Context: StarRocks-on-Sirius (GPU SQL engine embedded in a StarRocks compute node, "CN"). An SF1000 profiling campaign found four blockers; you are helping choose the best fix for one of them.
Read first: /home/prestouser/.claude/plans/sf1000-top4-fixes-plan.md (the plan: issues, candidate solutions, criteria, acceptance tests) and the relevant findings in /home/prestouser/.claude/plans/starrocks-sirius-perf/sf1000-planning-cardinality-backpressure.md (sections 3B, 3C, 4). Evidence bundle: /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/perf/sf1000 (WORKFLOW-PLAN.md indexes it; cn1-cnlog.txt, cn1-quent.txt, card-compare-*.txt, cn1/engine-cn0.log, cn1/dump/ are the raw material).
Source tree (read-only for you): /home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius-stacks-wt/perf (engine C++ under src/, CN Rust under experimental/starrocks/src, translator under experimental/starrocks/crates/starrocks-plan-translator, StarRocks FE Java under experimental/starrocks/starrocks/fe, engine docs under docs/super-sirius/).
Rules: do not modify the source tree, do not start clusters or GPU jobs, write only under /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/fix/designs/. Distinguish measured facts from inference. Cite file:line for every mechanism you rely on.

Issue: Per-query parked-output bookkeeping in the CN. Designs: /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/fix/designs/parked-bookkeeping-{surgical,robust,upstream}.md. Judges' verdicts: [
 {
  "scores": [
   {
    "angle": "surgical",
    "fixes_failure": 4,
    "correctness_risk": 4,
    "reviewability": 4,
    "effort": 5,
    "measurability": 4,
    "total": 21,
    "notes": "Fixes the measured 1-CN case in the campaign config (async dispatch, capture-cn.sh:12): the engine Err arm marks the query on the engine thread before the next dequeue, so q05's queued 5773/5777/5776/5775 (cluster.log 6072-6305), q17's aca1 (17884-17984, 6343 ms) and q21's acb are skipped, and the worker Err arm's abandon_query covers q16's translation failure (16593) with slots ff86/ff87 still parked. Verified against engine.rs:267-275, 278-318, 462-478, 697-717; compute_node_service.rs:380-390, 457-479, 864-911, 1358-1393; result_store.rs:163-212. Gaps, all unmeasured and none a regression vs today: (1) the skip is placed in the Run arm before run_fragment, so a skipped receiver carrying remote_inputs bypasses the lease sweep at engine.rs:462-478 and leaks staging-arena leases (4-CN only; arena exhaustion is a hard failure, B6); (2) no LocalExchange purge, and the non-goal text calls stale entries 'host-side KBs' but SenderSource::Remote { batches } (local_exchange.rs:36-47) holds arena leases released only when the receiver runs (engine.rs:671-679); (3) AbandonQuery is FIFO-only with no shared set, so in the default sync mode a cancel- or CN-triggered abandonment lets Runs already queued in the engine channel run to completion first (a 100 s lineitem scan at SF1000) - only the engine-Err trigger refuses them; (4) skipped fragments still emit 'fragment run started' (run_labeled :1540-1580), so the plan's literal acceptance line must be re-worded. Factual slip: '642 cancel_plan_fragment lines' is 321 cancel RPCs (each logged twice); all 321 carry query_id; reasons 5/1/3 = 192/72/57. The core per-query drop is testable only on GPU (engine.rs is behind the sirius-engine feature, lib.rs:51-52; CI runs --no-default-features, Cargo.toml:44-51). prost names confirmed: QueryFinished/LimitReach (target/.../out/starrocks.rs:3266-3272)."
   },
   {
    "angle": "robust",
    "fixes_failure": 5,
    "correctness_risk": 3,
    "reviewability": 3,
    "effort": 2,
    "measurability": 5,
    "total": 18,
    "notes": "Fixes the measured case in both dispatch modes: the shared `terminated` Arc is marked from the caller thread before the fire-and-forget DropQuery, so engine GATE 1 refuses Runs already queued ahead of it, and the CN gates in run_ready_fragment (:864) and run_labeled (:1540) meet the plan's literal 'no fragment run started' criterion; terminate on the inline RPC Err (:705-718, :1661-1675) and the rendezvous purge with lease release close the multi-CN holes. FE facts verified (DefaultCoordinator.java:1003-1035, 1048-1066, 1155-1177; BackendServiceClient.java:192-209; FragmentInstanceExecState.java:383-415; ExecutionDAG.java:620-646). Risks that contradict the 'correct under cancellation' claim as written: GATE 1 at dequeue skips before run_fragment, bypassing the remote-input lease sweep (engine.rs:462-478); the CN dispatch gate returns Vec::new() without releasing the Remote staged batches inside ready.inputs (3.5 does not mention it); the TTL timer thread must post EngineRequest::Sweep, and if it holds a plain Sender clone the channel never closes and Drop for SiriusEngine (engine.rs:853-870) hangs on join - needs recv_timeout or a stop flag, not discussed. Blast radius on the 15 passing queries is the largest of the three: every QUERY_FINISHED/LIMIT_REACH cancel (264 of 321 in cn1) now runs terminate_query (lifecycle.mark + DropQuery + remove_query + remove_receiver_instance) and inserts into `terminated`, which GATE 1/GATE 2 consult; fail_query_all changes the INTERNAL_ERROR cancel semantics that cancel_fails_only_a_waiting_entry (result_store.rs:490-510) pins; three new knobs, a TTL that can expire legitimate parked output, an Inventory request, a new enum crossing the FragmentExecutor seam, and a park/claim/release refactor guarded by two GPU tests. The AlreadyTornDown idempotent release is the one piece the other designs lack and should be merged. 3.5-4 days as three stacked PRs."
   },
   {
    "angle": "upstream",
    "fixes_failure": 5,
    "correctness_risk": 4,
    "reviewability": 4,
    "effort": 3,
    "measurability": 5,
    "total": 21,
    "notes": "Fixes the measured case in both dispatch modes and closes the multi-CN holes: engine Err retires on-thread; SiriusEngine::retire_query marks the shared RetiredQueries before the fire-and-forget RetireQuery so queued Runs are refused at dequeue; the refusal is placed inside run_fragment so the lease sweep at engine.rs:462-478 still runs (the only design that gets this right); refuse_if_retired in run_ready_fragment releases Remote staged batches in ready.inputs and emits no 'fragment run started' (plan wording met); fail_fragment on both dispatch paths covers q16 (translation at :1361) and the inline RPC Err (:704-717, :1661-1675); cancel retires for every reason (LIMIT_REACH included, closing the not-yet-run-receiver case the surgical gate argues away), records a failure only for non-internal reasons, and retire_receiver returns sources so leases are released; is_retired lets a late peer frame be released and acked. Verified against local_exchange.rs:87-95, 105-157, 248-313; result_store.rs:87-99, 127, 163-212; nixl_transport.rs:407-421, 786-790; proto internal_service.proto:464-482, 812-827. Weak spots: drop_parked keeps exactly-once, so the theoretical QUERY_FINISHED-vs-post-eos drop_parked race on a sender CN would fail a drain the FE no longer cares about (microsecond window; impossible in inline mode because the FE cannot finish while the sender RPC is open) - merge robust's AlreadyTornDown; RetiredQueries capacity 64 is small once every finished query is pushed (results.failure_of is the primary CN gate, so it is only a fallback - raise to 1024); the exchange's retired FIFO needs a HashSet alongside the VecDeque or is_retired is a linear scan per frame; every finished query now costs N empty RetireQuery sends and marks (safe by construction: at QUERY_FINISHED all fragments of the query on this CN have run, receiver-first materialisation B1); mechanical refactor of engine.rs park/claim/release guarded by two GPU tests plus the new CI registry tests; inline-path query-level recording is a documented behaviour change. No knobs, no timer, one PR with two Conventional Commits (~400 + 500 LOC), ~2 days."
   }
  ],
  "winner": "upstream",
  "reasoning": "Measured facts re-checked in the evidence: the six wipes and leftover runs (cn1/cluster.log 6050-6305, 16593-16605, 17711-17999, 21344-21617), base@start 4.69/8.83/31.56/38.16/4.00/36.64 GB (agent-notes/refute-oom5/headroom.txt), the 0.72/1.04/0.39/6.42/3.35 s of stolen engine time (notes.md, runs.csv), 321 cancel RPCs all with query_id (reasons 5/1/3 = 192/72/57), cn4 had zero failures. All three designs describe today's mechanism correctly (engine.rs:278-318 process-wide wipe; compute_node_service.rs:457-479 result-store-only cancel; :864-911 fail_query only; :1361 translation before slot extraction; local_exchange.rs removals only in take_ready :248-313). Every file:line I re-checked in the three designs is accurate; the only factual slip is the surgical design's 642 cancel lines (321 RPCs, each logged twice). B4's verdict holds: this fix changes no pass/fail, so 'fixes the measured failure' means removing the leak and the stolen time, which all three do for the campaign configuration.\n\nJudged from correctness: all three handle the primary engine-Err trigger in both dispatch modes because the engine thread marks the query before its next dequeue. They diverge on the other two triggers (CN-side failure, FE cancel) and on the multi-CN leases. The surgical design has no shared set, so in the default sync mode a cancel- or CN-triggered abandonment lets Runs already queued in the engine channel execute fully; it skips before run_fragment and so bypasses the remote-input lease sweep (engine.rs:462-478); and it leaves SenderSource::Remote staged batches (arena leases, not host KBs) pinned for dead queries. None of these regress the 1-CN measured case, so it is the safest smallest diff, but it does not meet the plan's literal acceptance line and does not close the multi-CN cancel gap the plan lists. The robust design fixes both triggers in both modes and adds idempotent release, but as written repeats the lease-sweep bypass at GATE 1 and in the CN dispatch gate, adds a timer thread whose Sender clone would defeat SiriusEngine's channel-close shutdown unless handled, and runs a teardown on every one of the 264 success-path cancels plus three knobs and a TTL that can expire legitimate output: the widest blast radius on the 15 passing queries and the most review load, for benefit the campaign cannot measure. The upstream design fixes all three triggers in both modes, is the only one that places the refusal inside run_fragment so the lease sweep runs and that releases staged batches on the CN-side skip, tears down the rendezvous with lease release on cancel, meets the plan's 'no fragment run started' criterion, and does it with no knobs in one two-commit PR. Its remaining holes (exactly-once drop_parked after a QUERY_FINISHED retire, FIFO capacity 64, linear is_retired) are small and fixed by merging two pieces of the robust design. Totals tie the surgical and upstream designs at 21; the correctness side breaks the tie for upstream because its extra ~300 lines buy default-mode and multi-CN correctness rather than surface area. No design is disqualified.",
  "merge_suggestions": "Base: upstream (registry + shared RetiredQueries + refusal inside run_fragment + fail_fragment on both dispatch paths + cancel teardown with rendezvous purge, two commits, commit 2 can be a stacked PR). Merge from robust: (1) ParkedRegistry::release on a retired slot returns Ok(AlreadyTornDown) exactly once and forgets the entry, so the transport's post-eos drop_parked (nixl_transport.rs:790) after a QUERY_FINISHED retire and its failure-path drop_parked (:412) after an INTERNAL_ERROR retire are not errors, while a second release of a live slot stays loud (keeps compute_node_service.rs:2703-2757 green); (2) the structured teardown line fields (trigger=engine_err|cn_err|cancel:<reason>, fragments, slots, still_parked) and an INFO 'skipping fragment of a retired query' line as the acceptance grep target; (3) the process_fragment refusal for a late deploy of a retired query (upstream already has it). Do not merge the TTL sweep, the three knobs, the Inventory request, fail_query_all, or the three-PR split. Merge from surgical: (1) RetiredQueries capacity 1024 with FIFO eviction instead of 64, since every finished query now enters it; (2) the unlabelled-failure GPU test and the cancel-reason matrix test (INTERNAL_ERROR/TIMEOUT/USER_CANCEL/None record a failure, QUERY_FINISHED/LIMIT_REACH do not; query_id None takes today's path) using a RecordingRetireExecutor; (3) its acceptance arithmetic (headroom.txt base@start 0.00, QueryBegin allocated at q17 == q16, client-start-to-first-fragment gap <= 100 ms for q06/q22). Implementation notes for the spec: give the exchange's retired FIFO a HashSet twin so is_retired is O(1) per frame; place both the engine and CN refusals so that Remote staged batches and remote_inputs leases are released (engine.rs:462-478 path, StagedBatch len > 0 rule at fragment_executor.rs:92-105); state explicitly that QUERY_FINISHED retires parked state but never touches ResultStore, guarded by a test that a repeat fetch_data still reports EOS; and record in the PR that the 4-CN cancel path is verified by a fault-injection arm (q16 between two passing queries), since the campaign's cn4 arm had no failures.",
  "disqualifiers": [
   "None of the three designs is unworkable as written; the following are must-fix items the implementer has to resolve, not disqualifiers.",
   "surgical: the failed-query skip sits in the Run arm before run_fragment, so a skipped receiver with remote_inputs never reaches the lease sweep at engine.rs:462-478 and pins staging-arena leases (4-CN only); move the check inside run_fragment or sweep the leases at the skip.",
   "surgical: section 2.5 calls stale LocalExchange entries 'host-side KBs', but SenderSource::Remote { batches } (local_exchange.rs:36-47) holds arena leases that are released only when the receiver runs (engine.rs:671-679); the non-goal is a real 4-CN leak, not a cosmetic one.",
   "surgical: cannot satisfy the plan's acceptance line 'no fragment run started for a dead query' (run_labeled :1540-1580 logs before executor.run); the orchestrator must accept the re-worded 'elapsed_ms <= 5 with the skipped marker' or require a CN-side gate.",
   "robust: GATE 1 at dequeue and the CN dispatch gate in run_ready_fragment are written to skip without releasing remote_inputs / ready.inputs staged batches, the same lease leak; the design text must add the release.",
   "robust: the TTL sweep timer thread posts into the engine request channel; if it holds a Sender clone, Drop for SiriusEngine (engine.rs:853-870) never sees the channel close and the process hangs on join - needs recv_timeout on the engine loop or a stop flag; not discussed in the design.",
   "upstream: drop_parked keeps exactly-once after a QUERY_FINISHED retire, so the sub-millisecond post-eos race on a sender CN would fail a drain of a finished query; merge robust's AlreadyTornDown release.",
   "factual (surgical): '642 cancel_plan_fragment lines for 66 runs' double-counts the tracing close lines; cn1/cluster.log has 321 cancel RPCs, all with query_id (reason 5: 192, reason 1: 72, reason 3: 57). Mechanism unaffected."
  ]
 },
 {
  "scores": [
   {
    "angle": "surgical",
    "fixes_failure": 4,
    "correctness_risk": 4,
    "reviewability": 5,
    "effort": 5,
    "measurability": 4,
    "total": 22,
    "notes": "Removes every measured 1-CN leak (4.69/8.83/31.56/+6.60/4.00/36.64 GB, headroom.txt base@start) and the 11.9 s of leftover-fragment time: engine-side Err marks the query on the engine thread before the next dequeue, so in the campaign's async mode (capture-cn.sh:12) 5773/5777/5776/5775 and q21's acb are skipped; the worker Err arm at compute_node_service.rs:877-897 covers q16's translation failure; reason-gated cancel (proto :464-471, generated starrocks.rs:3266-3271) keeps the 15 passing queries on an unchanged path (cancels are reason 5/1 only, cn1-cnlog.txt). Two as-written defects cost points. (1) The engine skip is placed at the Run dequeue (engine.rs:282-318) BEFORE run_fragment, so a skipped Run's remote_inputs never reach the lease sweep at engine.rs:462-478: on 4 CNs a dead query's receiver with staged batches in hand leaks its staging-arena leases for the process lifetime, which is a regression against today (today the leftover receiver runs and the push loop releases them). Fix is a placement change: put the check as the first statement inside run_fragment, exactly where the upstream design puts it. (2) No CN-side gate: in async mode a dead query's sender still goes through execute_ready_fragment -> translate -> run_labeled and emits 'fragment run started'/'fragment run failed' before the engine refuses it (the design's R9/R10), so the plan's literal acceptance line 'no fragment run started for a dead query' does not hold; the design substitutes elapsed_ms<=5 + a 'skipped' marker. The design also understates itself in R1/2.4: after an engine-side Err the engine-local FailedQueries is set before the next dequeue, so queued Runs in sync mode ARE skipped; only CN-side failures and cancels have the FIFO window. Core retain logic lives in cfg-gated engine.rs, so CI never runs it (lib.rs:51-52; experimental.yml:79); only the two GPU tests do. ~110 code + ~240 test lines, three files, one fork PR, half a day."
   },
   {
    "angle": "robust",
    "fixes_failure": 5,
    "correctness_risk": 3,
    "reviewability": 2,
    "effort": 2,
    "measurability": 5,
    "total": 17,
    "notes": "Covers everything measured plus the multi-CN cancel cleanup (rendezvous purge + staged-lease release), idempotent late drop_parked, TTL sweep, retention, telemetry, three knobs. Largest blast radius: every QUERY_FINISHED/LIMIT_REACH cancel of a passing query now runs terminate_query (engine DropQuery message per instance, 2-13 per query per cn1-cnlog.txt cancels=, exchanges.remove_query, remove_receiver_instance), release() semantics change (AlreadyTornDown is Ok, weakening the exactly-once contract the transport tests pin at compute_node_service.rs:2703-2757), GATE 2 discards a running fragment's output if the query was marked mid-run (a mis-mark loses live output), the TTL default (1800 s) can fail a legitimately long query, push_sender/register_receiver signatures change, and two terminated maps (engine + ServiceCore) must stay in sync. GATE 1 sits at the Run dequeue and therefore has the same lease-sweep bypass as the surgical skip, mitigated only by the CN-side gate and remove_query's lease release (a cancel racing an in-flight dispatch still leaks). PR 3 (sweep/knobs/docs) is scope beyond the measured problem: the FE already cancels every multi-instance query (DefaultCoordinator.java:1027-1034, measured cancels=N), so the accidental-sweep loss is covered without a timer. Three stacked fork PRs, 3.5-4 engineer-days; the stack's PR 2 alone touches compute_node_service.rs, local_exchange.rs and result_store.rs and is borderline for one sitting. Test plan is the best of the three (CI-tested registry, component tests in both dispatch modes, 4-CN smoke) and its acceptance greps match the plan literally."
   },
   {
    "angle": "upstream",
    "fixes_failure": 5,
    "correctness_risk": 4,
    "reviewability": 3,
    "effort": 3,
    "measurability": 5,
    "total": 20,
    "notes": "Covers the measured leaks and stolen time, q16, the inline-path failure recording, staged-lease release on refusal and on translation failure, cancel teardown (parked + rendezvous + late-frame refusal), with the dead-query check correctly placed INSIDE run_fragment so the lease sweep at engine.rs:462-478 still runs. Extracting ParkedRegistry<F> into a non-gated module makes the park/claim/release/retire bookkeeping CI-testable for the first time (engine.rs is never compiled in CI); RetiredQueries is an Arc<Mutex> marked by both the engine Err arm and SiriusEngine::retire_query, so already-queued Runs are refused in both dispatch modes. Correctness risk is moderate-low: the cancel path now acts on ALL reasons including QUERY_FINISHED (N fire-and-forget sends + N retire_receiver inserts per passing query; empty retires), and the inline RPC error path now records fail_query (a behaviour change the design owns). The theoretical QUERY_FINISHED-vs-post-eos drop_parked race is practically closed by FIFO ordering (DropParked is enqueued right after rpc_transmit returns at nixl_transport.rs:790, long before an FE round trip) and would only produce a spurious drain error on a finished query. Bounded consts (64/1024), no knobs. Roughly 400 non-test + 500 test lines across 6 source files + a new module, one PR in two commits (commit 2 can be stacked); ~2 engineer-days + one GPU session. The refactor of the relay/export/release path is mechanical but is what pushes it past a quick review. Acceptance greps ('skipping fragment of a retired query', no 'fragment run started' after 'fragment run failed', QueryBegin allocated within 1 MB of baseline) match the plan literally; the 4-CN arm with q16 as the deliberate failure is runnable with capture-cn.sh 4."
   }
  ],
  "winner": "surgical (with two mandatory merges from upstream: the engine-side skip moved inside run_fragment, and the CN-side dispatch gate in run_ready_fragment with Remote-lease release)",
  "reasoning": "Delivery-side judgement. All three designs rest on the same verified mechanisms (engine.rs:267-275/282-318/697-717 wipe and park; compute_node_service.rs:380-390 worker, :864-911 Err arm with fail_query at :896, :457-479 cancel stub, :1358-1362 translate-before-slots; result_store.rs query_failures consulted only in reserve :127; local_exchange.rs take_ready :248-313 as the only removal; FE per-instance cancels with query_id at BackendServiceClient.java:192-206 and QUERY_FINISHED/LIMIT_REACH only after eos at DefaultCoordinator.java:1027-1034) and the same measured evidence (headroom.txt base@start; cluster.log 6050-6305 for q05, 16585-16610 for q16; cn1-cnlog.txt cancels=N; refute-oom5/notes.md stolen time). B4 established this fix is hygiene and order-independence, not a pass/fail flip, so the value ceiling is fixed and the deciding criteria are blast radius, PR size, and how fast the acceptance arm runs. The surgical design gets the whole measured 1-CN effect in ~110 code lines in three files with a provably unchanged path for the 15 passing queries (no cancel-path change for reasons 5/1, one HashMap::get per Run), can be implemented in half a day in the already-built fix-parked-bookkeeping worktree (engine + CN built 15:51 today, GPUs idle now), and its smoke arm (q05 q06 q16 q17 q21 q22) runs in ~7 minutes with existing tooling (capture-cn.sh, run-queries.sh, headroom.txt, cnlog_extract.py). It is the '80% for 20%' version and the answer to whether a smaller version suffices is yes. It is not mergeable exactly as written: its Run-dequeue skip bypasses the remote-lease sweep at engine.rs:462-478 (a 4-CN staging-arena leak that today does not exist, because the leftover receiver runs and releases its leases), and without a CN-side gate the dead query's senders still translate and log 'fragment run started' before the engine refuses them, so the plan's literal acceptance wording fails. Both are fixed by lifting two small pieces from the upstream design (~20 lines): the check inside run_fragment, and refuse_if_retired at the top of run_ready_fragment reading the query_failures record that fail_query already writes, releasing SenderSource::Remote staged batches from ready.inputs. The upstream design is the best engineering of the three (CI-testable registry, correct check placement, both dispatch modes, cancel teardown closing the multi-CN staged-lease leak) and would be the right shape for an eventual dev-bound CN PR, but it is 3-4x the diff and ~2 days, and its extra coverage (rendezvous purge, late-frame refusal, inline-path recording) addresses paths the campaign did not measure; it fits better as the follow-up PR once fix 2's SF1000 arm is green. The robust design over-delivers against the measured problem (TTL sweep and three knobs for a case the FE's measured cancels=N already covers), changes the release contract and the cancel path for every passing query, spans three PRs and ~4 days, and its GATE 1 has the same lease-sweep bypass. Landing order, on which all three agree and which I endorse: land fix 2 before fix 1's SF1000 time-to-fail arm, because the 0.7-6.4 s of leftover-fragment time (q17->q18 6.42 s) would otherwise confound that measurement; no proto, FE, or engine C++ change, so no other dependency. Acceptance on this box: smoke ~7 min, full 22-query arm ~16 min today (~4 min once fix 1 lands); avoid the 02:00-03:50 UTC nightly window.",
  "disqualifiers": [
   "None of the three is disqualified outright; each works for the measured 1-CN failure. Two as-written defects must be corrected before merge: (a) surgical: the engine-side skip at the Run dequeue (engine.rs:282-318) bypasses run_fragment's remote-lease sweep (engine.rs:462-478), so on 4 CNs a refused Run that carries remote_inputs leaks its staging-arena leases for the process lifetime, a regression against today; move the check inside run_fragment (the upstream design's placement). (b) robust: GATE 1 at the Run dequeue has the same bypass; its CN-side gate and remove_query lease release cover most of it but a cancel racing an in-flight dispatch still leaks; same fix. The upstream design has no as-written defect; its only behaviour change worth a second look is acting on QUERY_FINISHED/LIMIT_REACH cancels for every passing query (N fire-and-forget sends and retire_receiver inserts), which is harmless by construction but is a change on the hot path the surgical gate avoids."
  ],
  "merge_suggestions": "Into the surgical design, mandatory: (1) from upstream, place the dead-query check as the first statement inside run_fragment (engine.rs:430-481) rather than at the dequeue, so the lease sweep at :462-478 runs for a refused Run; (2) from upstream, add ServiceCore::refuse_if_retired at the top of run_ready_fragment (:864) consulting a new ResultStore::failure_of(query_id) accessor over the query_failures map that fail_query already writes (result_store.rs:96-98, :163-200), logging 'skipping fragment of a retired query' and releasing SenderSource::Remote staged batches in ready.inputs via executor.staging_release (len > 0), so no 'fragment run started' is emitted for a dead query and the plan's acceptance grep holds literally; add the skips= column to cnlog_extract.py as upstream proposes. Recommended, not blocking: (3) from upstream, make the abandon/retain logic generic over the fragment type and host it in a small non-feature-gated module so the retain-only-this-query logic gets a CI test (engine.rs is never compiled in CI, experimental.yml:76-79); the full ParkedRegistry refactor can wait. (4) from upstream, release Remote staged leases in run_ready_fragment's Err arm for the translation-failure case at 4 CNs (today's ready.inputs are dropped on the floor at :1361-1362). Defer to a follow-up PR (upstream's commit 2 as a stacked PR): cancel_plan_fragment purging LocalExchange state by receiver instance with staged-lease release and late-frame refusal (closes the multi-CN arena leak the campaign did not measure), and the inline-path fail_query recording. Take from robust only if the 4-CN smoke ever shows a drop_parked-after-teardown error: the idempotent AlreadyTornDown release. Do not take the TTL sweep, retention knobs, GATE 2, or the release-contract change: the FE's measured per-instance cancels (cancels=N on every run) already give an event-driven sweep, and the plan's criterion 2 penalises hot-path changes for the 15 passing queries."
 }
]
Write the implementation spec /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/fix/designs/parked-bookkeeping-SPEC.md for an engineer who will implement it in a worktree without talking to you: goal and non-goals; exact mechanism with file:line anchors and the code shape (signatures, data structures, error text); tests to write first (names, what they assert, where they live: Catch2 under test/cpp/..., Rust #[cfg(test)] in the crate, FE JUnit); build and test commands for this repository (pixi run make, the CN cargo test recipe in experimental/starrocks/pixi.toml, fe-build for FE patches, and note the FE patch delivery via experimental/starrocks/patches + apply-starrocks-patches.sh); acceptance at SF1000 (what the orchestrator will run and what numbers must come out); risks and how the reviewer should probe them; landing order and dependencies on the other three fixes; commit message title (Conventional Commits). 13	| 1 | The OOM reschedule loop has no feasibility check | `src/pipeline/gpu_pipeline_executor.cpp` (:263 reservation gate, :330-420 reschedule, MAX_RETRIES=100, 50 ms sleep) | q05 q08 q09 q17 q18 q21 take 54-232 s to die (775 s of a 910 s sweep); 17,917 "0 bytes freed, proceeding with partial reservation" lines |
14	| 2 | No per-query parked-output bookkeeping | `experimental/starrocks/src/engine.rs` (:291-316 process-wide wipe on Err), `compute_node_service.rs` (:449-476 cancel is result-store only), `local_exchange.rs` (removals only in take_ready) | 0-38 GB of a dead query's parked output survives into later queries; dead query's queued senders still run (q22 cold 4110 vs 943 ms) |
15	| 3 | The FE plans every FILES() scan at 1 row | StarRocks FE `StatisticsCalculator.computeFileScanNode` (:664-676), `TableFunctionTable.java` (file sizes at :611, schema RPC), `PGetFileSchemaResult` (proto :647-650), CN `file_schema.rs` | every distribution decision is data-blind: 1 CN broadcasts 3.79B lineitem rows into q04's semi join, 4 CNs shuffle 3.23B rows for q03; all six failures are one plan shape |
16	| 4 | Six queries cannot run on 1 CN | fragment cut (FE) + receiver-first full materialisation (`engine.rs` run_fragment_inner, `local_exchange.rs`) + parked repositories outside the downgrade sweep (`src/exec/streaming_fragment.cpp:103-112`, `src/downgrade/downgrade_executor.cpp:223-300`) | q05 q08 q09 q17 q18 q21 OOM; standalone Sirius runs them in 2.7-6.5 s |
17	
18	## Candidate solutions to weigh (input to the design workflow, not the decision)
19	
20	1. **Fail fast.** (a) Abort at the reservation gate when `retry_count > 0 && freed == 0 && retry floor > grant`; (b) abort in the reschedule path when downgrade freed 0 and pool usage == limit and nothing completed since the previous attempt; (c) a bounded wall-clock/attempt budget per original task that scales with observed progress; (d) keep 100 retries for the batch-lock contention case (arrives via `rmm::out_of_memory` from `lock_or_prepare_batch`, not via the gate). Must produce an error that names parked bytes vs pool.
21	2. **Bookkeeping.** (a) `query_id` on every `ParkedOutput`, drop only the failing query's slots; (b) failed-query set on the engine thread that skips pending `Run`s; (c) `cancel_plan_fragment` drops the cancelled query's parked outputs and dequeues its fragments (needs a by-query removal in `LocalExchange`); (d) `drop_parked` in `run_ready_fragment`'s Err arm for pre-run translation failures; (e) a periodic sweep as a safety net. Order of landing matters: (a)+(d) are pure hygiene, (b)/(c) touch the dispatch contract.
22	3. **Cardinalities.** (a) FE-only: rows = total bytes / row width from the inferred schema in `computeFileScanNode`, using `TableFunctionTable` file sizes (no wire change; column stats stay UNKNOWN); (b) exact `num_rows` from parquet footers: new field in `PGetFileSchemaResult`, filled by the CN's `file_schema.rs` (proto + FE + CN); (c) later, per-column min/max from row-group stats; (d) no-FE alternative: CN-side translator refusal/hints, SQL join hints. Delivered as a patch in `experimental/starrocks/patches/` applied by `apply-starrocks-patches.sh`, so the FE must be rebuilt (`pixi run fe-build`). Predicted effect must be checked with `EXPLAIN COSTS` at 1 and 4 CNs: the source skeptic warns that `BROADCAST_JOIN_MEM_EXCEED_PENALTY` and zero single-node shuffle cost may still put lineitem across an exchange on 1 CN.
23	4. **Run the six on 1 CN.** (a) Same-node fragment fusion before translation: replace a receiver's `EXCHANGE_NODE` with its single local sender's node list at the `TPlan` level when every destination is this CN, so the fused plan is the standalone plan (needs `RIGHT_SEMI` in the translator for q21, finding P5); (b) spillable parked repositories: register streaming-sink outputs and receiver inputs with a registry the downgrade executor sweeps as a third tier, HOST-tier `output_row_count` and `export_packed` (five of six then fit in GPU+HOST = 279 GB; q09 marginal); (c) streaming receivers (build side first, probe streamed) is the long-term fix but touches the engine's single-flight lifecycle; (d) FE-side: real cardinalities (issue 3) may already move lineitem to the probe side of a broadcast join, which the engine can stream. The design must say which combination actually makes each of the six pass and what each costs.
24	
25	## Evaluation criteria (judges score 1-5 each)
26	
27	1. Does it fix the measured failure at SF1000 on this box (which queries, predicted numbers, how verified)?
28	2. Correctness risk and blast radius (which paths change for the 15 passing queries; determinism; cancellation).
29	3. Size and reviewability as an upstream PR (target layer in the carve plan: engine `src/` -> dev PR; CN `experimental/starrocks` -> fork PR; FE -> checked-in patch), tests it needs.
30	4. Effort and dependencies (what must land first; FE rebuild; proto change).
31	5. Measurability: an acceptance test that a reviewer can rerun in minutes plus the SF1000 arm.
32	
33	## Acceptance tests (must exist before implementation is "done")
34	
35	| fix | unit / component test | SF1000 verification (orchestrator-run, one arm at a time) |
36	|---|---|---|
37	| 1 | Catch2 test in `test/cpp/pipeline/` driving a task through the reschedule path with a memory space that never frees: query fails within a bounded number of attempts with the new error text; contention case still retries | 1 CN, q05 q08 q09 q17 q18 q21: time-to-fail <= 5 s each (was 54-232 s), error names parked bytes; the 15 passing queries unchanged (warm medians within noise, `compare.py` set unchanged) |
38	| 2 | Rust tests in `engine.rs`/`local_exchange.rs`/`compute_node_service.rs`: failure drops only that query's slots; queued senders of a failed query are skipped; cancel drops parked outputs; translation failure drops slots in hand | 1 CN sweep in the same order as before: `[gpu_pool] allocated` returns to baseline after each failure (was +4.7..+38 GB), q22 cold no longer inflated, no `fragment run started` for a dead query after its failure |
39	| 3 | FE unit test (Java) for the new statistics path; CN test if the proto changes; `EXPLAIN COSTS` golden outputs for q03 q04 q05 q22 at 1 and 4 CNs showing real cardinalities and the new join sides | 1 CN and 4 CN sweeps of the 15 passing queries plus the six: plan shapes recorded, timings vs the campaign table, oracle compares |
40	| 4 | Fusion: translator/CN tests that a single-destination local exchange fuses and the fused plan matches the sender+receiver plan; spill: Catch2 test that a parked repository is swept to HOST and relayed back | 1 CN: q05 q08 q09 q17 q18 q21 pass with oracle MATCH; report their times against standalone (2.7-6.5 s) |
41	
42	## Workflows
43	
44	**A. Design exploration (`fix/design-workflow.js`).** Per issue, three independent designers with different angles (surgical minimum, robust design, what upstream would accept), each reads the report finding, the evidence and the code and returns a design (mechanism, files, tests, risks, predicted effect). Two judges per issue score the three against the criteria and pick or merge. One synthesizer per issue writes the spec `scratchpad/fix/designs/<issue>-SPEC.md`. A final integrator checks the four specs for interactions (fail-fast vs bookkeeping ordering; fusion vs spill vs cardinalities) and writes the build order.

46	**B. Implementation (`fix/implement-workflow.js`).** Per issue in its own worktree: implementer (tests first, then code, build, run the unit tests; commits with Conventional Commits and the Claude trailer), adversarial reviewer, fixer, verifier (fresh build + tests + clippy/fmt/pre-commit). Agents never start clusters or use GPUs other than the one assigned to their worktree (fix 1: GPU 0, fix 2: GPU 1, fix 3: none, fix 4: GPU 2). The orchestrator then runs the SF1000 arms from the table above, one at a time, and an integration branch with all four for the final sweep.

# Fix 2, robust design: query-scoped teardown of parked output on the CN

Angle: the design a senior engineer ships for the long run. Correct under cancellation and
concurrent queries, observable, configurable where it must be, with the failure modes written
down. Source tree read at `/home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius-stacks-wt/perf` (branch
`perf/profile-sf1000`, 45dab3be); evidence at `scratchpad/perf/sf1000`. Every number is
**measured** (file named) or marked **inference**.

## 0. Summary

Today a query's parked sender output on a CN is released only by the receiver that consumes it.
When the query dies, three things go wrong (all measured on the 1-CN SF1000 sweep):

1. The engine thread's `Err` path wipes **every** parked output process-wide
   (`engine.rs:291-316`), which is collateral damage for any concurrent query and does not even
   help the failing one on 1 CN (see 4.1).
2. The dead query's not-yet-run senders keep running and park output nobody will consume
   (`dispatch_worker` has no notion of a dead query, `compute_node_service.rs:380-390`):
   0-36.64 GB leaked per failure, 0.39-6.42 s of engine-thread time stolen from the next query.
3. `cancel_plan_fragment` touches only the result store (`compute_node_service.rs:449-476`), and
   a failure that never enters the engine (translation, q16) drops nothing.

The design replaces the process-wide wipe with **one query-scoped teardown**,
`ServiceCore::terminate_query(query_id, cause)`, reachable from three triggers (a fragment
failure, an FE cancel, a TTL sweep) and acting on four subsystems (the engine's parked
registry, the dispatch path, the exchange rendezvous, the result store). Teardown is idempotent,
tolerates the transport's late `drop_parked`, refuses late `Run`s of the dead query at two gates,
logs one structured report per teardown, and has two knobs. It changes nothing on the hot path of
a healthy query beyond a hash lookup per fragment run.

## Tools (same dir)
explain_summary.py, cnlog_extract.py, card_compare.py, quent_bp.py, results_table.py, ../quent_summary.py (per-operator Computing sums)

## Facts established before the analysis
1. FE StatisticsCalculator.computeFileScanNode sets outputRowCount = 1 for FILES() scans ("we don't know the real schema in file, just use the default Row Count now"); every column statistic UNKNOWN. Hence every plan node has cardinality 1 and the CBO picks BROADCAST for most joins (orders 1.5B rows broadcast in q07/q09/q10..., lineitem 3.79B rows as the build side of q04's LEFT SEMI JOIN, partsupp 800M in q02).
2. Engine stream ids == FE exchange node ids; the receiver declares the exact parked row count per stream before build() ("declared input stream cardinality"), so DuckDB plans the receiver fragment with exact input cardinalities, but only after every sender finished (receiver-first rendezvous, local_exchange.rs). Nothing streams across a fragment boundary: the whole intermediate is parked on the GPU.
3. Engine OOM handling: gpu_pipeline_executor.cpp reschedules a task on OOM up to MAX_RETRIES=100 with a 50 ms sleep, then fails the query ("exceeded maximum retry limit"). It does not wait for memory to be released and cannot spill parked batches. q05 and q08 died this way on 1 CN at SF1000 (GPU_SCAN OOM, 101 s and 168 s).
4. Reserving.requested_bytes / peak_estimate vs Computing.peak_allocated_bytes (Quent task FSM) measure the engine's own memory estimation; standalone SF10 q01 requested 20.8 GB for a 5.6 GB peak.

## Analysis dimensions (workflow)
A. Planning: per query, FE fragment tree and join distribution vs the DuckDB/Sirius standalone plan; what a stats-aware FE would choose; where the translator/CN could override (e.g. swap build/probe, refuse broadcast above a row threshold, local re-planning of a broadcast join once the actual parked cardinality is known).
B. Cardinality: FE estimate vs actual rows per exchange (card_compare), engine reservation estimate vs peak (quent_bp), the receiver-first exact-cardinality mechanism and its cost.
C. Backpressure: parked bytes and dwell per fragment, staging lease held/in-transit time and max concurrency vs SIRIUS_EXCHANGE_STAGING_BYTES, Reserving/Queued waits, OOM reschedule storms, nixl transmit lease_ms/write_ms, 1-CN vs 4-CN scaling per query, standalone vs CN.
Each per-query analysis is verified adversarially (two skeptics with different lenses); the synthesis ranks findings with the evidence lines and proposes changes with file paths and confidence.

8. Translator comment (node_translator.rs ~1924-1931) already records that the FE reports cardinality 1 for every FILES() scan and that nothing bounds a join build side; "bounding it belongs to the executor".

The engine's DuckDB optimizer runs on every fragment (sirius_ffi.cpp:135, with STATISTICS_PROPAGATION and a few rewrites disabled, :233-240); the declared stream cardinality feeds the TableFunction cardinality callback (stream_bind_catalog.hpp:44-46), so build/probe choice inside a fragment sees exact stream sizes, but FILES() scans inside the same fragment carry DuckDB's parquet estimate. Session-wide per CN ~3700 leases, max 94 concurrent (arena = 16 GiB).

The gate only canonicalizes row order inside the update-phase aggregate; the FE plan computes the revenue CTE twice (two independent two-phase aggregations over FP64-lowered decimals) and then joins on `total_revenue = max(total_revenue)`. Batch arrival order into the merge phase (and therefore FP64 summation order) still varies run to run, so the two sums can differ in the last bits and the equality join yields nothing. 1	# Fix 2, upstream angle: per-query parked-output bookkeeping in the CN
2	
3	Design written 2026-09-03 for the SF1000 plan (`~/.claude/plans/sf1000-top4-fixes-plan.md`, issue 2) from
4	the angle "what the maintainers of sirius-db/sirius would accept as one reviewable CN PR". Source tree read
5	at `/home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius-stacks-wt/perf` (branch `perf/profile-sf1000` = 45dab3be); every
6	`file:line` below is from that tree. Evidence root: session scratchpad `perf/sf1000/`. "Measured" means
7	copied from a named evidence file; everything else is marked inference.
8	
9	## 1. The defect, restated from the code and the log
10	
11	Four independent mechanisms let a dead query's output survive on the GPU and let its fragments keep
12	running after the query has already failed.
13	
14	### 1.1 The engine thread wipes every parked output, process-wide, when any run fails
15	
16	`experimental/starrocks/src/engine.rs:44-47` (the parked record has no owner):
17	
18	```rust
19	struct ParkedOutput<'ctx> {
20	    fragment: sirius::Fragment<'ctx>,
21	    outstanding: usize,
22	}
23	```
24	
25	`engine.rs:267-268, 291-316` (the Err arm):
26	
27	```rust
28	let mut parked: HashMap<u64, ParkedOutput<'_>> = HashMap::new();
29	let mut parked_slots: HashMap<SenderSlot, (u64, u64)> = HashMap::new();
30	...
31	if let Err(err) = &result {
32	    // ... The wipe is process-wide, so it also destroys OTHER in-flight fragments'
33	    // parked output. Record why, and say so out loud ...
34	    poisoned.clear();
35	    for slot in parked_slots.keys() {
36	        poisoned.insert(slot.clone(), err.clone());
37	    }
38	    parked.clear();
39	    parked_slots.clear();
40	}
41	```
42	
43	The wipe is also the *only* place parked memory of a failed query is released, so anything parked
44	after the wipe by the same dead query is never released (1.2).
45	
46	### 1.2 Fragments of a failed query keep running and re-park output nobody consumes
47	
48	`compute_node_service.rs:380-390` (dispatch worker: FIFO, one at a time, no liveness check):
49	
50	```rust
51	fn dispatch_worker(core: Arc<ServiceCore>, inbox: mpsc::Receiver<ReadyFragment>) {
52	    while let Ok(ready) = inbox.recv() {
53	        let mut queue = vec![ready];
54	        while let Some(ready) = queue.pop() {
55	            queue.extend(core.run_ready_fragment(ready));
56	        }
57	    }
58	}
59	```
60	
61	`compute_node_service.rs:864-911` records the failure at query level (`self.results.fail_query(query_id,
62	id, error)` at :896) but nothing reads that record on the sender path: `run_ready_fragment`,
63	`process_fragment` (:918-951) and `run_labeled` (:1540-1581) never consult `results.query_failures`
64	(`result_store.rs:98`, documented as "First failure recorded per query. A result fragment that reserves
65	*after* the failure landed fails immediately" and used only in `reserve`, :127).
66	
67	**Measured, q05 on 1 CN** (cn1/cluster.log after ANSI stripping; the capture ran with
68	`SIRIUS_CN_ASYNC_SENDER_DISPATCH=1`, `perf/sf1000/capture-cn.sh:12`): the lineitem sender
69	`...5774` failed at 13:05:24.626 after 101,193 ms (`fragment run failed`, line 6051), the engine logged
70	`discarding every parked sender output on this CN after a fragment failure slots=2` (line 6050), the worker
71	attributed it with `fail_query` (line 6052), and then ran the same dead query's queued senders `5773`
72	(started 13:05:24.632012, line 6072, 8 ms), `5777` (33 ms), `5776` (582 ms) and the receiver `5775`
73	(`inputs=2 outputs=1`, 73 ms, lines 6181-6305). The FE's first `cancel_plan_fragment` for the query
74	arrived at 13:05:24.632266 (line 6073), 0.25 ms after `5773` had started. `5775` and `5776` parked output
75	that no receiver ever consumed; it survived until q08's failure wiped it.
76	
77	### 1.3 Cancel is a result-store-only stub
78	
79	`compute_node_service.rs:457-479`:
80	
81	```rust
82	async fn cancel_plan_fragment(&self, request: PCancelPlanFragmentRequest, ...) {
83	    let id = FragmentInstanceId::from(&request.finst_id);
84	    info!(..., "acknowledging cancel_plan_fragment (best-effort: no engine-side abort yet)");
85	    ...
86	    self.core.results.cancel(id, reason);
87	    Ok(PCancelPlanFragmentResult { status: Self::ok_status() }.into())
88	}
89	```
90	
91	The FE sends one cancel per fragment instance with the real instance id and the query id
92	(`fe-core/.../qe/scheduler/dag/FragmentInstanceExecState.java:404-406`,
93	`rpc/BackendServiceClient.java:192-206` fills `finstId`, `queryId`, `cancelReason`, `errorMessage`), with
94	reason `INTERNAL_ERROR` on failure (`qe/DefaultCoordinator.java:768-784 handleErrorExecution`) and
95	`QUERY_FINISHED` or `LIMIT_REACH` after the last result batch (`DefaultCoordinator.java:1027-1033`).
96	Measured: 11 cancels with `cancel_reason=3` for q05's 11 instances (cluster.log 6073-6094); `cancels=N`
97	equal to the fragment count for every passing query (`perf/sf1000/cn1-cnlog.txt`, e.g. `q02.r0 ...
98	frags=13 ... cancels=13`). On this CN a cancel frees nothing and dequeues nothing.
99	
100	### 1.4 A pre-run failure loses the slots (and remote leases) already in hand
101	
102	`compute_node_service.rs:1325-1394 execute_ready_fragment` translates first (:1361-1362) and only then
103	extracts the `LocalParked` slots and `Remote` staged batches out of `ready.inputs` (:1363-1392). A
104	translation error returns before the engine sees the slots, so nothing calls `drop_parked` for them and
105	nothing releases the remote batches' staging leases. `run_ready_fragment`'s Err arm (:875-909) only
106	records the failure.
107	
108	**Measured**: q16 failed at translation ("multi_distinct_count has a partial state this translator does
109	not model", plan fact 5) after its partsupp scan had parked; `agent-notes/refute-oom5/headroom.txt` shows
110	`q16.r0 ... base@start 31.56 ... max_alloc 38.16` and `q17.r0 base@start 38.16`: the 6.60 GB parked by
111	q16 was carried into q17 and never released by anything but q17's own failure wipe.
112	
113	### 1.5 What it cost at SF1000 (measured, `agent-notes/refute-oom5/headroom.txt`, GB at the first fragment of a run)
114	
115	| after failure of | carried into | `base@start` |
116	|---|---|---|
117	| q05 | q06.r1..q07.r2 | 4.69 |
118	| q08 | q09 | 0.08 (q08's wipe cleared it; the 8.83 GB the report attributes lands inside q09) |
119	| q09 | q10.r1..q16 (seven queries) | 31.56 |
120	| q16 (translation) | q17 | 38.16 (= 31.56 + 6.60) |
121	| q17 | q18 | 0.00 at q18 start, 4.0 GB inside (B4) |
122	| q21 | q22.r0 5.94 during, q22.r1/r2 | 36.64 |
123	
124	Engine-thread time spent on dead queries' fragments after their failure (B4): q17 -> q18 6.42 s, q21 -> q22
125	~3.35 s, q08 -> q09 1.04 s, q05 -> q06 0.70 s (8 + 33 + 582 + 73 ms from lines 6097-6305). q22 cold
126	4110 ms vs 971/915 ms warm (`cn1-cnlog.txt` lines 50-52).
127	
128	B4's verdict stands: no pass/fail at SF1000 was decided by the leak. This fix is hygiene, order
129	independence of the sweep, and the missing cleanup for the multi-CN cancel path. It does not make any of
130	the six failing queries pass.
131	
132	## 2. Design
133	
134	One CN PR, no engine C++ change, no FE patch, no proto change, no new environment knob.
135	
136	### 2.1 Principle
137	
138	*The engine holds parked state; the CN decides when a query is over.* The engine thread learns that a
139	query is over from two sources only: its own `Err` for a run of that query (immediately, on the same
140	thread, before it dequeues the next request), and an explicit `retire` request from the CN (for
141	pre-run failures and FE cancels). Every retirement is scoped to one query id, taken from the
142	`FragmentLabel` every run already carries (`fragment_executor.rs:57-63`; set from the FE params in
143	`compute_node_service.rs:1584-1589 fragment_label`).
144	
145	### 2.2 New module `experimental/starrocks/src/parked_registry.rs` (CI-compiled, no `sirius` dependency)
146	
147	The three loose maps and free functions in `engine.rs` (`parked`, `parked_slots`, `poisoned` at
148	:267-275; `missing_slot` :369-377; `export_next` :380-403; `release_slot` :408-425; the park block
149	:697-717) move into one generic struct so the bookkeeping is unit-testable without a GPU. `engine.rs` is
150	behind `#[cfg(feature = "sirius-engine")]` (`src/lib.rs:51-52`) and CI builds `--no-default-features`
151	(`Cargo.toml:44-51`), so today none of this logic runs in CI.
152	
153	```rust
154	/// One parked sender fragment and who still has a claim on it.
155	struct Parked<F> {
156	    fragment: F,
157	    /// The StarRocks query this output belongs to (`None` for unlabeled test runs).
158	    query_id: Option<FragmentInstanceId>,
159	    /// Destinations that have not yet released their stream.
160	    outstanding: usize,
161	}
162	
163	pub(crate) struct ParkedRegistry<F> {
164	    parked: HashMap<u64, Parked<F>>,
165	    slots: HashMap<SenderSlot, (u64, u64)>,
166	    /// Why a slot's output went away: filled by `retire`, replaced (never accumulated) on the
167	    /// next retirement. Same bound and same message contract as today's `poisoned`.
168	    poisoned: HashMap<SenderSlot, String>,
169	    next_id: u64,
170	}
171	
172	impl<F> ParkedRegistry<F> {
173	    /// Park once; each destination claims (id, stream i). Refuses a duplicate slot before
174	    /// inserting anything (today's engine.rs:697-717 contract).
175	    pub fn park(&mut self, query_id: Option<FragmentInstanceId>, outputs: &[SenderSlot], fragment: F)
176	        -> Result<(), String>;
177	    /// The parked fragment and stream a slot names (engine.rs:625-631 relay lookup, :386-392 export).
178	    pub fn claim(&mut self, slot: &SenderSlot) -> Result<(&mut F, u64), String>;
179	    /// Read-only lookup used by the cardinality declaration (engine.rs:559-566).
180	    pub fn peek(&self, slot: &SenderSlot) -> Option<(&F, u64)>;
181	    /// Exactly-once release of one destination's claim (engine.rs:408-425).
182	    pub fn release(&mut self, slot: &SenderSlot) -> Result<(), String>;
183	    /// Drops every parked fragment of `query_id`, poisons its slots with `cause`, returns
184	    /// (fragments dropped, slots dropped). Idempotent: a second call returns (0, 0).
185	    pub fn retire(&mut self, query_id: Option<FragmentInstanceId>, cause: &str) -> (usize, usize);
186	    pub fn len(&self) -> usize;
187	}
188	
189	/// Queries this CN has declared over, so a run that was already queued for one of them is refused
190	/// instead of re-parking output nobody will consume. Bounded FIFO; a StarRocks query id is never
191	/// reused, so eviction only forgets an explanation, never a live query.
192	pub(crate) struct RetiredQueries {
193	    order: VecDeque<FragmentInstanceId>,
194	    causes: HashMap<FragmentInstanceId, String>,
195	}
196	impl RetiredQueries {
197	    pub const CAPACITY: usize = 64;
198	    pub fn mark(&mut self, query_id: FragmentInstanceId, cause: String);
199	    pub fn cause(&self, query_id: FragmentInstanceId) -> Option<&str>;
200	}
201	```
202	
203	The `poisoned` message changes from "was discarded when another fragment on this CN failed" to
204	"was discarded when its query was retired: {cause}"; the generic "no parked sender output to {verb} for
205	{slot:?}" stays (engine.rs:369-377 contract, relied on by `engine_pushes_staged_remote_batches`
206	:1200-1203 which only asserts `is_err()`).
207	
208	### 2.3 `engine.rs`: scoped retirement, refusal of dead runs, a retire request
209	
210	* `engine_thread` (:242-363) owns `ParkedRegistry<sirius::Fragment<'_>>` (declared after `context`
211	  for the drop order the comment at :262-266 requires) and an `Arc<Mutex<RetiredQueries>>` shared with
212	  the `SiriusEngine` handle, in the same way the handle already serves `staging` off-thread (:129-138;
213	  the "one shared C++ allocator, two entry points" precedent). The shared set is what lets a cancel
214	  refuse runs that are already queued in the request channel ahead of it; the channel is FIFO
215	  (`std::sync::mpsc`, :151) and a queued `Run` of a dead query would otherwise execute for its full
216	  duration (a lineitem scan at SF1000: 101 s) before any retire message reached the thread.
217	
218	* Err arm (:291-316) becomes:
219	
220	```rust
221	if let Err(err) = &result {
222	    retire(&mut registry, &retired, request.label.query_id, err);
223	}
224	```
225	
226	  with
227	
228	```rust
229	fn retire(registry: &mut ParkedRegistry<_>, retired: &Mutex<RetiredQueries>,
230	          query_id: Option<FragmentInstanceId>, cause: &str) {
231	    let (fragments, slots) = registry.retire(query_id, cause);
232	    if let Some(query_id) = query_id {
233	        retired.lock().mark(query_id, cause.to_string());

534	## 6. Risks and how the design bounds them
535	
536	1. **Refusing a run the FE still wants.** Only three events mark a query retired: the engine's own Err for
537	   that query, a recorded CN failure of that query, or an FE cancel for it. All are terminal on the FE side
538	   (`DefaultCoordinator.java:1048-1066`: a cancelled query cannot be cancelled twice and receives no new
539	   dispatches). `QUERY_FINISHED`/`LIMIT_REACH` retire parked state but record no failure, so a repeat
540	   `fetch_data` still sees EOS.
541	2. **Retiring a query whose remote drains are in flight** (same query, this CN is a sender): the transport
542	   thread's next `export_packed_next` fails with the retiring cause, its `drop_parked` warns (:412-418),
543	   and the RPC reports a failure the FE already knows. Today's wipe does the same to *every* query's drain.
544	3. **Refactor of the park/claim/release path.** Mechanical move of existing code into `ParkedRegistry`;
545	   covered by the two existing GPU tests and the new CI tests. Keep the `poisoned` replace-never-accumulate
546	   rule and its bound (engine.rs:308-313).
547	4. **Loss of the accidental sweep.** A parked output whose receiver never arrives and whose query never
548	   fails was, until now, freed by the next unrelated failure. With per-query scoping it stays until the
549	   FE's end-of-query cancel, which every multi-instance query receives (`DefaultCoordinator.java:1027-1033`;
550	   measured `cancels=N` for all 15 passing queries). Single-instance queries get no cancel but also have
551	   no exchange and park nothing.
552	5. **Bounded memories.** `RetiredQueries` (64) and the exchange's `retired` FIFO (1024) are `const`s, not
553	   knobs; eviction forgets an explanation (a later drain gets the generic "no parked sender output") or, for
554	   the exchange, lets a very late frame re-create a source (today's behaviour). Query ids never recur.
555	6. **Inline-path recording is a behaviour change**: an inline sender failure now also fails the query's
556	   result instances reserved on this node with the real cause instead of the 600 s long-poll timeout. This
557	   is the documented reason `SIRIUS_CN_ASYNC_SENDER_DISPATCH` is off by default (:284-288); the fix does not
558	   forward failures to other nodes, so that note stays true.
559	7. **Both dispatch modes must be tested** (the campaign ran with async on; the default is off); the CI
560	   tests run each relevant case in both modes.
561	8. **Fire-and-forget `RetireQuery`** loses its error return; the engine thread logs failures. The only
562	   failure mode is a closed channel (shutdown), when there is nothing left to drop.

590	## 9. What this design deliberately does not do
591	
592	* No periodic sweep or timer (plan item 2e): the FE's per-instance end-of-query cancels already give a
593	  bounded, event-driven sweep; a timer would need a knob and a doc row.
594	* No `query_id` on the wire frame or on `ExchangeKey`: per-instance retirement matches the FE's per-instance
595	  cancels and the exchange's existing keying.
596	* No preemption of a fragment already executing inside the engine (`Fragment::run` is synchronous; the
597	  engine's single-flight lifecycle, `sirius_context.cpp:1555-1596`, is B1's problem, not this fix's).
598	* No eviction of drained `ResultStore` entries or cached descriptor tables (`result_store.rs:250-254`,
599	  `compute_node_service.rs:196-197`); pre-existing TODO, separate PR.
600	* No forwarding of a sender failure to the receiver's node (the reason async dispatch is off by default).

94	## 2. Mechanism
95	
96	One idea: **the engine thread remembers which queries failed and owns "abandon query" as a
97	primitive**; the two CN call sites that learn about a failure (the dispatch worker's `Err` arm and
98	the FE's non-success cancel) invoke that primitive. Everything else follows from FIFO ordering on
99	the existing engine channel.
100	
101	### 2.1 `engine.rs`
102	
103	**(a) Tag parked output with its query.** `ParkedOutput` (`engine.rs:44-47`) gains
104	`query_id: Option<FragmentInstanceId>`, copied from `request.label.query_id` at park time
105	(`engine.rs:710-716`). `FragmentLabel.query_id` is already carried on every `ExecuteRequest`
106	(`engine.rs:72`, `fragment_executor.rs:58-63`) and set by `fragment_label` for every FE-dispatched
107	fragment (`compute_node_service.rs:1584-1589`).
108	
109	**(b) A failed-query memory on the engine thread.** Next to `parked` / `parked_slots` / `poisoned`
110	(`engine.rs:267-275`), a `FailedQueries` value: `HashMap<FragmentInstanceId, String>` (id -> first
111	cause) plus a `VecDeque` for FIFO eviction at 1024 entries. Query ids are 128-bit unique, so a stale
112	entry can only ever match a fragment of the query that failed, and an evicted entry can only matter
113	if a fragment of a query that failed 1024 failures ago is still pending, which the FE's 300 s query
114	timeout rules out.
115	
116	**(c) Skip pending runs of a failed query.** In the `Run` arm (`engine.rs:282-318`), before
117	`run_fragment`:
118	
119	```rust
120	if let Some(query_id) = request.label.query_id
121	    && let Some(cause) = failed_queries.get(&query_id)
122	{
123	    let _ = request.respond.send(Err(format!(
124	        "fragment of query {query_id} skipped: the query already failed on this CN: {cause}"
125	    )));
126	    continue;
127	}
128	```
129	
130	No `context.fragment()`, no `build()`, no GPU work, no park. The error text carries the original
131	cause, so a result fragment skipped this way still names the real failure through `fetch_data`
132	(and `ResultStore::fail_query` keeps the first cause anyway, `result_store.rs:174-179`).
133	
134	**(d) Drop only the failed query's parked output.** Replace the body of the `Err` arm
135	(`engine.rs:301-315`) with a call to one function that both the `Err` arm and the new request use:
136	
137	```rust
138	/// Drops every parked output of `query_id` (all of them when the failure carried no query id,
139	/// which is today's process-wide wipe) and remembers the failure so later `Run`s of the query
140	/// are skipped. Returns the number of parked fragments dropped.
141	fn abandon_query<'ctx>(
142	    parked: &mut HashMap<u64, ParkedOutput<'ctx>>,
143	    parked_slots: &mut HashMap<SenderSlot, (u64, u64)>,
144	    poisoned: &mut HashMap<SenderSlot, String>,
145	    failed_queries: &mut FailedQueries,
146	    query_id: Option<FragmentInstanceId>,
147	    cause: &str,
148	) -> usize {
149	    if let Some(query_id) = query_id {
150	        failed_queries.insert(query_id, cause.to_string());
151	    }
152	    let doomed: HashSet<u64> = parked
153	        .iter()
154	        .filter(|(_, output)| query_id.is_none() || output.query_id == query_id)
155	        .map(|(park_id, _)| *park_id)
156	        .collect();
157	    if doomed.is_empty() {
158	        return 0;
159	    }
160	    // Same bound as today: only the most recent abandonment explains a missing slot.
161	    poisoned.clear();
162	    parked_slots.retain(|slot, (park_id, _)| {
163	        let keep = !doomed.contains(park_id);
164	        if !keep {
165	            poisoned.insert(*slot, cause.to_string());
166	        }
167	        keep
168	    });
169	    parked.retain(|park_id, _| !doomed.contains(park_id));
170	    doomed.len()
171	}
172	```
173	
174	`Err` arm becomes: log at `warn!` with `query_id`, `slots`, `error` ("discarding the failed
175	query's parked sender outputs"; the old wording stays for the `query_id: None` wipe), then
176	`abandon_query(..., request.label.query_id, &err)`. The `missing_slot` attribution
177	(`engine.rs:365-377`) is unchanged and still names the culprit.
178	
179	**(e) One new request.** `EngineRequest::AbandonQuery { query_id: FragmentInstanceId, cause: String }`
180	with **no respond channel**: its two callers must never wait behind a running fragment (the
181	cancel RPC runs on the BRPC current-thread runtime; the module doc at `engine.rs:16-21` records the
182	q02 wedge that motivates the rule). Handler: `abandon_query(..., Some(query_id), &cause)` plus the
183	same `warn!`. FIFO on the existing channel gives the ordering the design relies on: a `Run` queued
184	before the `AbandonQuery` executes and parks, then gets dropped; a `Run` queued after is skipped.
185	
186	### 2.2 `fragment_executor.rs`

188	One trait method with a default:
189	
190	```rust
191	/// Best-effort, non-blocking: forget every parked output of `query_id` and refuse its later
192	/// runs. Called when the CN learns a query is dead (a fragment failed before or during its
193	/// run, or the FE cancelled it for a non-success reason). Unlike `drop_parked` this is a
194	/// sweep, not an exactly-once release, so an executor that parks nothing succeeds trivially.
195	fn abandon_query(&self, query_id: FragmentInstanceId, cause: String) -> Result<(), String> {
196	    let _ = (query_id, cause);
197	    Ok(())
198	}
199	```

201	`SiriusEngine` implements it by sending `EngineRequest::AbandonQuery` and returning without
202	receiving (an `Err` only when the channel is closed, i.e. shutdown). `StubExecutor` and every test

206	
207	**(f) Dispatch-worker failure.** In `run_ready_fragment`'s `(Some(id), Some(query_id))` arm

211	if let Err(err) = self.executor.abandon_query(query_id, error) {
212	    tracing::warn!(query_id = %query_id, error = %err, "could not abandon the failed query's parked output");

216	This covers every CN-side pre-run failure that leaves inputs parked: translation
217	(`:1361-1362`, the q16 case), "exchange senders produced different output names" (`:1347`), the
218	sink validations (`:1066-1131`), a posted-drain failure (`:872`, `:160-163`). For an engine-side
219	`Err` it is redundant and idempotent.
220	
221	**(g) FE cancel for a non-success reason.** In `cancel_plan_fragment` (`:457-479`), keep the
222	existing `results.cancel(id, reason)` and add:
223	
224	```rust
225	use crate::proto::starrocks::PPlanFragmentCancelReason as CancelReason;
226	let reason_code = request
227	    .cancel_reason
228	    .and_then(|code| CancelReason::try_from(code).ok());
229	let query_finished = matches!(
230	    reason_code,
231	    Some(CancelReason::QueryFinished | CancelReason::LimitReach)
232	);
233	if !query_finished
234	    && let Some(query_id) = request.query_id.as_ref().map(FragmentInstanceId::from)
235	    && let Err(err) = self.core.executor.abandon_query(query_id, reason.clone())
236	{
237	    warn!(query_id = %query_id, error = %err, "could not abandon the cancelled query's parked output");
238	}

240	
241	(prost variant names per the generated enum, `target/.../out/starrocks.rs:3266`.) `QUERY_FINISHED`
242	and `LIMIT_REACH` are the two reasons the FE sends for a query whose rows it has; a missing or
243	unknown reason is treated as a failure (the existing cancel test at `:3414-3460` sends
244	`cancel_reason: None` with an "exceed big query cpu limit" message and `query_id: None`, so it
245	still reaches no engine call). The FE sends one cancel per instance, so a dead 11-fragment query
246	produces 11 `AbandonQuery` messages; each is a `HashMap` scan of a map that is empty after the first,
247	microseconds on the engine thread.
248	
249	Why the gate is safe rather than merely conservative: in this CN's single-batch result model
250	(`result_store.rs:245-283`) the FE can only be at `QUERY_FINISHED`/`LIMIT_REACH` after the result
251	fragment ran, and a receiver runs only after every sender it reads has parked or staged
252	(`local_exchange.rs:248-280`), so at that moment nothing of the query is parked on any CN; an
253	`AbandonQuery` would find nothing. Gating simply avoids the engine message on every passing query.

255	### 2.4 Behaviour under the measured cases
256	
257	**q05 (engine-side failure on the worker).** 5774's `Run` returns `Err` at 13:05:24.627 ->
258	`abandon_query(Some(q05), ...)` drops the 2 parked slots (as today) and records q05. 5773's `Run`
259	(sent 5 ms later by the worker) is skipped without touching the GPU; so are 5777, 5776 and the
260	receiver 5775 (which today relayed 11 batches and parked 4.69 GB). `run_ready_fragment` logs each
261	skip and calls `fail_query` (no-op: first failure wins) and `abandon_query` (no-op: nothing
262	parked). The 11 FE cancels with reason 3 each queue an `AbandonQuery` that finds nothing. q06's
263	first fragment starts as soon as the worker reaches it: `QueryBegin allocated=0` instead of
264	4,690,817,280 bytes, and ~0.7 s earlier.
265	
266	**q16 (CN-side translation failure).** `ff87` and `ff86` park (6.6 GB). `ff85`'s translation fails
267	on the worker -> `fail_query` -> `abandon_query(Some(q16), "malformed plan ...")` -> the engine drops
268	both parked outputs and records q16. Pool returns to the pre-q16 baseline before q17 starts (today
269	+6.60 GB).

271	**q21 -> q22.** `acc` (179 ms) and `acb` (3153 ms, 36.6 GB parked) are skipped; q22's first
272	fragment starts ~3.35 s earlier with `allocated=0` instead of 36.64 GB.
273	
274	**Sync dispatch mode (default, `SIRIUS_CN_ASYNC_SENDER_DISPATCH` unset).** Senders run inside
275	their RPC threads and may already be queued on the engine channel ahead of the failing `Run`'s
276	return. Those already-queued `Run`s still execute and park (as today), then the `AbandonQuery`
277	sent by the FE cancel (or the worker's `Err` arm) drops what they parked. End state is clean; the
278	stolen time is bounded by fragments that were already queued at the failure, and every `Run` queued
279	after the `Err` is skipped by the failed-query memory. The campaign ran with async dispatch on
280	(`capture-cn.sh:12`), where the worker sends one `Run` at a time and nothing is queued ahead.
281	
282	**The 15 passing queries.** The `Run` arm does one `HashMap::get` on an empty map; the park stores
283	one `Option<FragmentInstanceId>`; the `Err` arm never runs; `run_ready_fragment`'s `Err` arm never
284	runs; every cancel carries reason 5 or 1 and takes the unchanged path. No engine message is added,
285	no ordering changes, no determinism change. The only visible difference is the cancel log line
286	gaining the decoded reason.

288	### 2.5 Explicit non-goals (and why they are safe to leave)
289	
290	- **`LocalExchange` removal by query.** A dead query's `PendingReceiver` (a cloned
291	  `TExecPlanFragmentParams`, KB-scale host memory) and its `SenderSource::LocalParked` references
292	  stay in the rendezvous maps (`local_exchange.rs:87-95`). The GPU bytes they refer to are gone
293	  (dropped by query id), the receiver can never become ready (its failed sender never pushed), and
294	  if a leftover sender of the dead query did complete a set, the readied receiver's `Run` is
295	  skipped by the failed-query memory before it relays anything. Host-side KBs per failed query;
296	  not the measured GB-scale defect. Can be a follow-up with a `query_id` in `PendingReceiver`.
297	- **Aborting a fragment that is currently running.** The engine's single-flight lifecycle
298	  (`sirius_context.cpp:1555-1596`, per report B1) has no abort; that is fix 1's territory

409	## 6. Risks
410	
411	| # | risk | why it is bounded |
412	|---|---|---|
413	| R1 | Sync dispatch mode: `Run`s already queued on the engine channel at failure time still execute and park | Bounded to fragments whose RPCs arrived before the failure (all of a query's RPCs arrive within ~100 ms of each other, B1); they are dropped by the `AbandonQuery` that follows; every later `Run` is skipped. Measured config (async on) has nothing queued ahead. No regression vs today. |
414	| R2 | Replacing the process-wide wipe removes the accidental "next failure cleans the last leak" safety net | Every path that can leave parked output unreachable now abandons the query explicitly: engine `Err` (d), worker pre-run `Err` (f), FE cancel for failures detected anywhere (g). Enumerated in section 2.4. The unlabelled case keeps the wipe. |
415	| R3 | Cancel gate misses a reason under which output is still parked | For `QUERY_FINISHED`/`LIMIT_REACH` nothing of the query is parked by construction (section 2.3); every other reason abandons. Regression-neutral: today nothing is dropped on any cancel. |
416	| R4 | `AbandonQuery` dropping a slot mid remote drain (4 CN) | Same as today's wipe: the next `export_packed_next` returns the poisoned cause, the drain fails, the transport's `drop_parked` warns (`nixl_transport.rs:409-418`). The FE already knows the query is dead. |
417	| R5 | Skipped result fragment reports "skipped ..." instead of the original error | `fail_query` keeps the first cause per query (`result_store.rs:174-179`) and the skip text embeds the original cause anyway. In sync mode a skipped sender's RPC returns INTERNAL_ERROR; the FE is already cancelling and ignores a second cancel (`DefaultCoordinator.java:1056-1058`). |
418	| R6 | `poisoned` growth | Cleared and refilled on every abandonment that drops something, exactly today's bound (`engine.rs:308-313`). |
419	| R7 | `FailedQueries` growth or a false skip | Capped at 1024 with FIFO eviction; ids are unique, so a false positive is impossible and a false negative needs a fragment pending across 1024 failures (> FE timeout). |
420	| R8 | Fire-and-forget send on a closed channel | `Err` returned and logged at warn; only at shutdown. |
421	| R9 | A `Run` interleaving with `AbandonQuery` | Impossible: both are handled by the single engine thread between requests; a running fragment lives on the stack, not in `parked`, and is abandoned when it parks (it is dropped by the later `AbandonQuery` or, if the failure came first, skipped). |
422	| R10 | Log noise: a skipped fragment still emits `fragment run started` / `fragment run failed` from `run_labeled` (`:1549-1578`) and an `error!` in `run_ready_fragment` | Cosmetic; the acceptance grep uses the `skipped` marker and `elapsed_ms`. A one-line `ResultStore::query_failure` check in `run_labeled` could silence it later; deliberately not in this change (second mechanism for the same predicate). |

1	# Fix 2, robust design: query-scoped teardown of parked output on the CN
2	
3	Angle: the design a senior engineer ships for the long run. Correct under cancellation and
4	concurrent queries, observable, configurable where it must be, with the failure modes written
5	down. Source tree read at `/home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius-stacks-wt/perf` (branch
6	`perf/profile-sf1000`, 45dab3be); evidence at `scratchpad/perf/sf1000`. Every number is
7	**measured** (file named) or marked **inference**.
8	
9	## 0. Summary
10	
11	Today a query's parked sender output on a CN is released only by the receiver that consumes it.
12	When the query dies, three things go wrong (all measured on the 1-CN SF1000 sweep):
13	
14	1. The engine thread's `Err` path wipes **every** parked output process-wide
15	   (`engine.rs:291-316`), which is collateral damage for any concurrent query and does not even
16	   help the failing one on 1 CN (see 4.1).
17	2. The dead query's not-yet-run senders keep running and park output nobody will consume
18	   (`dispatch_worker` has no notion of a dead query, `compute_node_service.rs:380-390`):
19	   0-36.64 GB leaked per failure, 0.39-6.42 s of engine-thread time stolen from the next query.
20	3. `cancel_plan_fragment` touches only the result store (`compute_node_service.rs:449-476`), and
21	   a failure that never enters the engine (translation, q16) drops nothing.
22	
23	The design replaces the process-wide wipe with **one query-scoped teardown**,
24	`ServiceCore::terminate_query(query_id, cause)`, reachable from three triggers (a fragment
25	failure, an FE cancel, a TTL sweep) and acting on four subsystems (the engine's parked
26	registry, the dispatch path, the exchange rendezvous, the result store). Teardown is idempotent,
27	tolerates the transport's late `drop_parked`, refuses late `Run`s of the dead query at two gates,
28	logs one structured report per teardown, and has two knobs. It changes nothing on the hot path of
29	a healthy query beyond a hash lookup per fragment run.
30	
31	Predicted effect on the SF1000 1-CN sweep: the six post-failure leaks (4.69 / 8.83 / 31.56 /
32	+6.60 / 4.00 / 36.64 GB) become 0; the ~11.9 s of leftover-sender time (q05->q06 0.72,
33	q08->q09 1.04, q09->q10 0.39, q17->q18 6.42, q21->q22 3.35 s) disappears; q22 cold drops from
34	4110 ms to about 1.0-1.2 s; the 15 passing queries are unchanged (their QUERY_FINISHED cancels
35	tear down an empty registry).
36

162	### 2.4 Rendezvous: removals only when a receiver becomes ready
163	
164	`local_exchange.rs:248-313 take_ready` is the only place `receivers`, `sources` and `remote_seq`
165	shrink. A receiver whose senders never all arrive, or a sender whose receiver never registers,
166	stays forever; a `Remote` source's `StagedBatch`es hold staging-arena leases

170	### 2.5 What the FE sends
171	
172	`fe/fe-core/.../rpc/BackendServiceClient.java:192-209`: every cancel carries `finst_id`,
173	`cancel_reason`, `query_id` (always set) and `error_message` (non-empty only for
174	INTERNAL_ERROR). `qe/DefaultCoordinator.java:1003-1035`: on `getNext` failure ->
175	`dealStatusToTryRetry` -> `cancelInternal(INTERNAL_ERROR)`; on eos with >1 instance ->
176	`cancelInternal(QUERY_FINISHED)` or `LIMIT_REACH` (`:1028-1034`); `:1161-1177
177	cancelRemoteFragmentsAsync` calls `cancelFragmentInstance` for **every** deployed execution
178	(`FragmentInstanceExecState.java:383-415`: only DEPLOYING/EXECUTING instances are sent; the CN
179	accepts every dispatch immediately, so all are EXECUTING). Phased schedule uses
180	`ExecutionDAG.cancelQueryContext` (`:620-646`) with a dummy `finst_id (0,0)` per worker.
181	Proto: `gensrc/proto/internal_service.proto:464-482` (`LIMIT_REACH=1, USER_CANCEL=2,
182	INTERNAL_ERROR=3, TIMEOUT=4, QUERY_FINISHED=5`). The FE does not wait for the cancel reply
183	(`cancelPlanFragmentAsync` returns a `Future` that `cancelFragmentInstance` discards), but a slow
184	reply on the shared jprotobuf channel misattributes later replies (docstring at
185	`compute_node_service.rs:449-454`), so the cancel handler must keep returning immediately.
186	
187	Consequence for the design: on 1 CN, cancel arrives **after** the next leftover sender has
188	already started (0.25 ms late in q05), so Err-time bookkeeping on the CN is mandatory and cancel
189	is the second line; on N CNs, cancel is the only signal a *sender-side* CN gets that a query
190	failing on another CN is dead.

192	## 3. The design
193	
194	### 3.1 One entry point, three triggers, four subsystems
195	
196	```
197	trigger                     ServiceCore::terminate_query(query_id, cause)      subsystem action
198	------------------------    -------------------------------------------      --------------------------------
199	run_ready_fragment Err  ->  1. lifecycle.mark(query_id, cause)          ->  dispatch gate: later Runs skipped
200	process_fragment Err        2. executor.terminate_query(query_id,cause) ->  engine: mark + DropQuery (async)
201	cancel_plan_fragment    ->  3. exchanges.remove_query(query_id)         ->  rendezvous purged; staged leases
202	   (INTERNAL_ERROR,            + remove_receiver_instance(finst_id)         released via staging_release
203	    TIMEOUT, USER_CANCEL)   4. results.fail_query / nothing              ->  FE-polled ids fail (or untouched)
204	cancel_plan_fragment    ->  same, with cause = Finished (release-only)
205	   (QUERY_FINISHED,
206	    LIMIT_REACH)
207	TTL sweep (engine)      ->  engine-local drop_query + warn; CN lifecycle learns it on next touch
208	```
209	
210	`TerminationCause` is an enum, not a string: `Failed { fragment: FragmentInstanceId, error }`,
211	`Cancelled { reason: PPlanFragmentCancelReason, message: Option<String> }`,
212	`Finished { reason }` (QUERY_FINISHED / LIMIT_REACH), `Expired { idle: Duration }`. `Display`
213	renders the text that today's `missing_slot` (`engine.rs:369-377`) and the FE error carry.
214	
215	### 3.2 Engine thread: `ParkedRegistry`, a terminated set, two gates
216	
217	Extract the three maps at `engine.rs:267-275` into `experimental/starrocks/src/parked.rs`:
218	
219	```rust
220	pub(crate) type QueryId = FragmentInstanceId;
221	
222	/// Everything the engine thread knows about parked sender output. Generic over the fragment
223	/// handle so the bookkeeping is unit-tested without a GPU (`F = ()` or a drop counter).
224	pub(crate) struct ParkedRegistry<F> {
225	    parked: HashMap<u64, ParkedOutput<F>>,
226	    slots: HashMap<SenderSlot, (u64, u64)>,
227	    by_query: HashMap<Option<QueryId>, Vec<u64>>,           // park ids per query
