232	pub(crate) struct TornDown { pub query_id: Option<QueryId>, pub cause: Arc<TerminationCause>, pub at: Instant }
233	
234	impl<F> ParkedRegistry<F> {
235	    pub fn park(&mut self, query_id: Option<QueryId>, label: FragmentLabel, slots: &[SenderSlot], fragment: F) -> Result<(), String>; // duplicate-slot refusal as today (engine.rs:703-707)
236	    pub fn get_mut(&mut self, slot: &SenderSlot) -> Result<(&mut F, u64 /*stream*/), SlotError>;  // SlotError::TornDown(cause) | Missing
237	    pub fn release(&mut self, slot: &SenderSlot) -> Result<Release, String>; // Release::Freed | Release::Outstanding(n) | Release::AlreadyTornDown
238	    pub fn drop_query(&mut self, query_id: Option<QueryId>, cause: Arc<TerminationCause>) -> DropReport; // moves slots to torn_down
239	    pub fn expire(&mut self, ttl: Duration, now: Instant) -> Vec<(Option<QueryId>, DropReport)>;
240	    pub fn inventory(&self) -> Inventory; // queries, slots, batches (via a caller-supplied fn on F)

246	Semantics that differ from today, each deliberate:
247	
248	- **`release` on a torn-down slot returns `Ok(Release::AlreadyTornDown)`** and removes the
249	  `torn_down` entry, so the transport's post-eos `drop_parked` (`nixl_transport.rs:790`) after a
250	  QUERY_FINISHED teardown, or its failure-path `drop_parked` (`:412`) after an INTERNAL_ERROR
251	  teardown, is not an error. A second release of a *live* slot stays a loud error (the
252	  exactly-once contract the transport tests pin, `compute_node_service.rs:2703-2757`).
253	- **`get_mut` (export / relay) on a torn-down slot returns `SlotError::TornDown(cause)`**,
254	  rendered as today's "sender output for {slot} was discarded when ... : {cause}" text so the
255	  q08-for-weeks diagnosis lesson (`engine.rs:270-275`) is kept, now naming the query and trigger.
256	- `torn_down` is bounded by time (`forget_torn_down_older_than(retain)`, default 600 s, run from
257	  the sweep) instead of "replace on next wipe".
258	
259	The engine thread (`engine_thread`, `engine.rs:242-363`) gets:

266	    if let Some(cause) = request.label.query_id.and_then(|q| terminated.lock().get(&q).cloned()) {

379	### 3.5 Dispatch gates on the CN side
380	
381	- `run_ready_fragment` start: `if let Some(cause) = self.lifecycle.check(query_id) { info!(query_id, fragment_instance_id, %cause, "skipping fragment of a terminated query"); return Vec::new(); }`.
382	  This is what removes the leftover senders in async mode (they sit in the worker's inbox).
383	- `run_labeled` (`:1540-1581`), just before `self.executor.run(run)`: the same check, so a
384	  sender running inline in its RPC (default mode) is refused with
385	  `Err("fragment of terminated query ...")` instead of touching the engine. RPC threads already
386	  blocked in `engine_call` are caught by engine GATE 1.
387	- `process_fragment` for a **new** fragment of a terminated query (the FE's deploy of a late
388	  level racing its own cancel): refuse with the cause. The FE ignores the error (its
389	  `queryStatus` is already non-OK, `DefaultCoordinator.java:1056-1058`).

391	### 3.6 Cancel semantics by reason
392

394	|---|---|---|

Result store untouched (a `Pending` entry the FE has not drained must not be failed). 406	### 3.7 Rendezvous: `LocalExchange::remove_query` / `remove_receiver_instance`
407	
408	`local_exchange.rs`: `PendingReceiver` gains `query_id: Option<QueryId>` (from
409	`params.params.query_id`, computed by the caller and passed to `register_receiver`);
410	`push_sender` gains a `query_id` argument (the sender's own, available at
411	`compute_node_service.rs:1193-1203`) recorded in `receiver_query: HashMap<FragmentInstanceId, QueryId>`.
412	Remote frames carry no query id on the wire (`internal_service.proto:812-827`), and none is
413	needed: the FE deploys receiver-first and waits for the level's replies before deploying senders
414	(`Deployer`, report P4), so the receiver is registered before its first frame; and every cancel
415	names the instance, so `remove_receiver_instance(finst_id)` purges any orphan `sources` entry
416	without a query mapping. `take_ready` keeps its removals; `remote_seq` is purged alongside.
417	
418	```rust
419	pub(crate) struct PurgedRendezvous { pub receivers: usize, pub sources: Vec<SenderSource> }
420	pub(crate) fn remove_query(&self, query_id: QueryId) -> PurgedRendezvous;
421	pub(crate) fn remove_receiver_instance(&self, id: FragmentInstanceId) -> Vec<SenderSource>;
422	```
423	
424	### 3.8 Sweep: the safety net for a silent FE
425	
426	A `std::thread` timer posts `EngineRequest::Sweep` every `min(ttl/4, 60 s)`; the engine thread
427	drops parked output whose query has had no touch (park, relay, export, frame) for
428	`SIRIUS_CN_PARKED_TTL_SECS` (default 1800; 0 disables) and warns once at `ttl/2`. The TTL must
429	exceed the FE's `query_timeout` (300 s default) by a wide margin because a receiver legitimately
430	waits for the slowest sender of its query. The sweep is the only path that frees memory when the
431	FE dies without cancelling, and it also prunes `torn_down`/`terminated` retention
432	(`SIRIUS_CN_TERMINATED_RETAIN_SECS`, default 600, bounded so a late deploy of a dead query is still
433	refused). Knobs go through `tunable.rs` (`Knob` with name/default/min/max, reject-not-clamp,
434	logged at bring-up; `tunable.rs:1-60`).
435

453	## 4. Behaviour under the measured cases
454	
455	### 4.1 The 1-CN SF1000 sweep, failure by failure
456	
457	The process-wide wipe was **not** the leak on 1 CN: at every wipe only the failing query's own
458	slots were parked (one query at a time), so today's `parked.clear()` and the new `drop_query`
459	free the same bytes. What changes is what happens next:
460	
461	| transition | today (measured) | with the design |
462	|---|---|---|
463	| q05 -> q06 | 5773/5777/5776/5775 run 13:05:24.632-25.355 (0.72 s), 5775 relays streams 1+4 and parks 4.69 GB that survives q06/q07 | engine `Err` at 13:05:24.626 marks q05 terminated on the engine thread; `run_ready_fragment` marks it on the CN and the worker's next pop (5773) is skipped with `skipping fragment of a terminated query`; 5777/5776/5775 likewise; the 11 cancels at .632 find q05 already torn down (idempotent). q06 starts at once; pool at q06 QueryBegin = 0.00 GB |
464	| q08 -> q09 | 6 leftovers 13:08:29.792-30.680 (1.04 s), 8.83 GB into q09 | skipped; 0 GB; q09's lineitem sender starts with a clean pool |
465	| q09 -> q10..q16 | 4 leftovers (0.39 s), 31.56 GB parked through 7 queries (21 runs); 47-178 ms reservation-gate blocks in q10/q12/q14 | skipped; 0 GB; the gate blocks in C3 lose their cause (**inference**: up to 0.18 s per q10/q12/q14 warm run recovered) |
466	| q16 (translation failure of receiver ff85) | senders ff86/ff87 parked 6.6 GB never dropped (no engine `Err`); +6.6 GB into q17 | `run_ready_fragment` `Err` -> `terminate_query(q16, Failed)` -> engine `DropQuery` frees ff86/ff87 within the same millisecond (engine idle) |
467	| q17 -> q18 | aca2 + aca1 (6.34 s scan) run after the failure, 4.0 GB into q18 | skipped: q18's timer starts 13:14:56.823 and its first fragment can start at ~.83 instead of 13:15:03.243 (6.42 s earlier) |
468	| q21 -> q22 | 2acc + 2acb (3.15 s, parks 36.64 GB) run after the failure; q22 cold 4110 ms, warm runs carry 36.64 GB | skipped; q22 cold = its own 0.755 s of fragments + FE head (~0.2 s, P4) + first-touch: predicted 1.0-1.2 s; warm 943 ms unchanged |
469	
470	Note the 0.25 ms race in q05: sender 5773 started **before** the first cancel ack. The design
471	does not depend on cancel for this; the CN marks the query at `run_ready_fragment`'s `Err`, which
472	executes on the dispatch worker *before* it pops 5773. In default (inline) mode the same senders
473	are RPC threads blocked in `engine_call`; engine GATE 1 refuses them because the engine thread
474	marked the query at its own `Err` before responding.

476	### 4.2 The 15 passing queries (1 CN and 4 CN)
477	
478	Per fragment run: one `HashMap` lookup in `run_ready_fragment`/`run_labeled`, one in engine
479	GATE 1, one in GATE 2, one `by_query` insert on park. Per query: 2-13 QUERY_FINISHED cancels
480	(`cn1-cnlog.txt cancels=`), each a `terminate_query(Finished)` that finds an empty registry
481	(every parked output was consumed before the result fragment could run, by construction of the
482	receiver-first rendezvous, B1) and logs at INFO. On 4 CNs a QUERY_FINISHED cancel can arrive on a
483	sender CN while the transport thread has transmitted eos but not yet called `drop_parked`
484	(`nixl_transport.rs:774-790`); `release` returns `AlreadyTornDown` and the drain reports success.
485	No plan, memory, or ordering change for these queries; warm medians should be within noise
486	(compare.py set unchanged).

488	### 4.3 Cases the campaign did not exercise
489	
490	- **User `KILL` mid-run** (USER_CANCEL while the engine is inside the query's fragment): cancel
491	  marks + posts `DropQuery`; the running fragment cannot be aborted (engine limitation, B3), but
492	  GATE 2 drops its output instead of parking, the CN never registers it, and every other fragment
493	  of the query is skipped. Memory returns as soon as the fragment ends.
494	- **Failure on another CN**: that CN's `run_ready_fragment` `Err` -> `fail_query` there; FE
495	  cancels every instance everywhere with INTERNAL_ERROR; this CN's parked output for the query
496	  (waiting on a drain, or already drained but the peer receiver died) is dropped by the cancel;
497	  an in-flight drain's next `export` fails with the teardown cause; staged remote frames for a
498	  receiver of the dead query on this CN are purged and their leases released (today they pin the
499	  arena forever, B6-adjacent).
500	- **FE dies, no cancel**: the sweep frees the output after `SIRIUS_CN_PARKED_TTL_SECS` and warns
501	  at half that; `parked_inventory` shows what is waiting.
502	- **Late deploy of a dead query** (FE level in flight when the failure happened): refused at
503	  `process_fragment` while the retention entry lives (600 s); after retention, it would register
504	  a receiver that never completes and be swept by the TTL.
505	
506	## 5. Failure modes of the design itself
507	
508	| # | scenario | what happens | why acceptable |
509	|---|---|---|---|
510	| F1 | QUERY_FINISHED cancel races the transport's post-eos `drop_parked` | `release` -> `AlreadyTornDown` (Ok) | test 7.5; without it a finished query's sender RPC would report an error |
511	| F2 | INTERNAL_ERROR cancel during an in-flight drain | next `export_packed_next` -> `Err(TornDown cause)`; drain fails; sender RPC / `fail_query` reports the teardown cause, not "no parked sender output" | the query is dead; the message names the culprit (the q08 lesson) |
512	| F3 | `terminate_query` for a query with a fragment mid-run on the engine | cannot abort; output dropped at GATE 2 when it ends | documented limitation; engine abort is fix-1/B3 territory |
513	| F4 | FE never sends cancel (crash) | TTL sweep frees after `SIRIUS_CN_PARKED_TTL_SECS` | default 1800 s >> FE query_timeout 300 s; knob |
514	| F5 | TTL too low for a legitimately long query (many-minute sender at SF10000) | its receiver fails with "sender output ... expired after N s" | loud, names the knob; warn at ttl/2 gives operators a signal first |
515	| F6 | Two failures of the same query (engine `Err` then CN `Err` then cancel) | `mark` keeps the first cause; later triggers log at DEBUG with `already_terminated=true` | idempotent by construction |
516	| F7 | Query id absent on the run (translate-only fixtures) | parked under `None`; only an `Err` of a `None` run drops the `None` bucket; never swept by query | preserves today's semantics for anonymous fragments |
517	| F8 | `DropQuery` posted while the engine is shutting down | `send_nowait` returns Err, logged; `Drop for SiriusEngine` drops the registry with the context (`engine.rs:359-361`) | nothing leaks past process exit |
518	| F9 | `staging_release` of a purged remote batch fails (arena gone) | warned, teardown continues | same tolerance as `engine.rs:470-476` |
519	| F10 | `terminated`/`torn_down`/`lifecycle` growth | bounded by retention (600 s) and by the sweep | one entry per query, pruned |
520	| F11 | A CN with async dispatch OFF and a sender RPC that failed at `route_destination` before running | `process_fragment` `Err` -> `terminate_query` | consistent: the FE fails the query on any RPC error |
521	| F12 | Knob `SIRIUS_CN_TEARDOWN_ON_CANCEL=0` | cancel reverts to `results.cancel`; Err-time and sweep paths still active | escape hatch only for the cancel contract |

676	## 10. Risks
677	
678	1. **Cancel contract drift.** The design assumes StarRocks sends QUERY_FINISHED only after the FE
679	   has every row (`DefaultCoordinator.java:1022-1035`). It does, and the CN's single-batch model
680	   means all parked output is consumed by then; the knob `SIRIUS_CN_TEARDOWN_ON_CANCEL` is the
681	   escape hatch. Mitigation: test 7.2.6/7.2.8 and the 4-CN smoke assertion `slots=0` on finished
682	   teardowns.
683	2. **Refusing a fragment the FE still expects.** `process_fragment` refusal of a late deploy of a
684	   terminated query returns an RPC error to an FE that has already failed the query -- harmless.
685	   If retention were shorter than the FE's deploy window the late fragment would register and be
686	   swept by the TTL instead; 600 s is far above any deploy.
687	3. **GATE 2 discards work.** Output of a fragment that finished after its query was terminated is
688	   dropped rather than parked; that is the intent, but a mis-marked query (a bug in a trigger)
689	   would lose a live query's output loudly ("terminated while running"). First-cause-wins and
690	   the cause text make such a bug diagnosable in one log line.
691	4. **TTL misconfiguration** (F5) can fail a long-running legitimate query; the default is 6x the
692	   FE query timeout and the warn-at-half gives a signal first. Set to 0 to disable in bring-up
693	   experiments.
694	5. **Engine backlog.** `DropQuery` is FIFO behind whatever the engine thread is doing; for a
695	   cancel during a 100 s fragment of the same query, the release happens when that fragment ends
696	   (F3). No new blocking anywhere.
697	6. **Interaction with fix 4(b) (spillable parked repositories).** If parked repositories get
698	   registered with the downgrade executor, dropping a `Fragment` must unregister them; flag to
699	   that design. Row counting already tolerates a spilled batch (`.ok()`).
700	7. **Behavioural change for the inline sender path**: a queued sender of a dead query now returns
701	   an RPC error instead of running; the FE already treats the query as failed, and
702	   `dispatched_receiver_failure_surfaces_through_fetch_data`-style tests cover the surfaced text.

303	**Measured** (engine-cn0.log `[gpu_pool] allocated` at fragment boundaries, agent-notes/refute-oom5/headroom.txt `base@start`): after q05 4.69 GB carried through q06/q07; after q08 8.83 GB into q09; after q09 31.56 GB through q10..q16 (seven queries); +6.6 GB from q16's parked partsupp scan -> 38.16 GB at q17's start; after q17 4.0 GB into q18; after q18 0; after q21 36.64 GB into q22 (q22 cold 4110 ms vs 943 warm). cluster.log shows the dead query's queued senders starting after `fragment run failed` (q05: 5773, 5777, 5776, 5775 at 13:05:24.632+, the first 0.25 ms before the FE's first cancel ack). Engine-thread time stolen from the next query: q17 -> q18 6.42 s, q21 -> q22 ~3.35 s, q08 -> q09 1.04 s.
304	
305	**Objection (both skeptics).** "Directly caused q17 to die with only 66 GB of its own data parked" is arithmetically false: q17's F00 lineitem projection is ~120-122 GB (46 tasks x 2.65 GB; standalone `GPU_SCAN(3) n=46 in=122.25 GB`), above the 107.37 GB cap, so it fails with zero leak; the leak only moved the death from ~40 to 25 parked batches. Every passing query that ran under a leak passed with `oom_resched=0` (q06/q07 under 4.69 GB, q10-q15 under 31.6-38.2 GB, q22 under 36.6 GB). No pass/fail in this campaign was decided by the leak. The order-dependence risk is real but inferred: q07's own parked footprint is 79.17 GB; under the 38.16 GB leak it would need ~117 GB and would have failed had it run between q09 and q17. The cn1 timings of q10-q16 and q22.r1/r2 were taken with 31.6 / 36.6 GB of the pool occupied (the reservation-gate blocks in C3 need that leak to occur).
306	
307	**Proposed (small, high confidence as hygiene).** Store `query_id` with each `ParkedOutput`; on `Err` drop only that query's slots; keep a failed-query set on the engine thread and skip its pending `Run`s (Err-time bookkeeping, since cancel arrives after the next sender already started); make `cancel_plan_fragment` drop the cancelled query's parked outputs and dequeue its fragments (needs a `LocalExchange` removal by query; today removals happen only in `take_ready`, local_exchange.rs:284-308); in `run_ready_fragment`'s Err arm `drop_parked` the slots already in hand when translation fails.
308	
309	#### B5 (confirmed, proposals corrected). Shuffle drains are serialised after the fragment finishes, and 84-88% of each drain is `export_packed` on the engine thread at ~63 GB/s
310	
311	**Measured, cn4 q03.r1** (cn4/cluster.log): each lineitem sender finished at +0.610..0.684 s, then performed 3 sequential transmits of 4.82-4.89 GB, each `elapsed_ms=92-98 lease_ms=1-2 write_ms=6-8` (600-717 GB/s write), completing at +95/+190/+283 ms after finish; the next fragment on that CN (customer scan) started 0.1-0.3 ms after the last transmit on all 4 CNs. Same pattern in q03.r0/r2 and in q10.r1 (lineitem 0.145-0.159 s, customer 0.083-0.102 s), q12.r1 (0.115-0.125 s), q19.r1 (0.055-0.078 s). The Quent staging-lease probe times the pack directly: 48-52 sender-side leases per CN of ~311 MB, pack median 4.9 ms per lease = 63.5 GB/s, non-pack (lease RPC + write + transmit RPC) 0.7 ms, so pack = 84-88% of the drain for q03 (74-82% q10/q12, 18-32% q19 with 7 MB batches). Receiver-side unpack of the same frames: 0.14 ms per 303 MB (2.1 TB/s), ~30x faster than the pack.
312	
313	**Source (verified).** `compute_node_service.rs:1207-1219` comment: "one FIFO request channel into ONE transport thread ... the drains still run one at a time, in the FE's destination order"; `:380-392 dispatch_worker` is one thread; `:864-872 run_ready_fragment ... .and_then(FragmentOutcome::join_into_ready)` joins the drains before yielding; `nixl_transport.rs:713-775` drain loop (`export_packed_next` per batch, lease RPC, `write_and_wait`, transmit RPC); `engine.rs:813 export_packed_next = engine_call` served by the single engine thread (engine.rs:321-324); `src/sirius_ffi.cpp:~800 kPackChunkBytes = 8 MiB` with `cudf::chunked_pack` on the default stream (~37 `next()` launches per 311 MB batch). The serialisation on the dispatch worker exists because `SIRIUS_CN_ASYNC_SENDER_DISPATCH=1` was set (capture-cn.sh:12; default off); with the default, the same drain holds the RPC open and delays the FE's next deploy stage instead (`Deployer.java:236-243, 318`). Either way it is on the critical path.
314	
315	**Corrections to the proposals.** More transport threads (b) or a non-joining dispatch worker (c) cannot deliver the claimed saving on their own: packs and fragment `Run`s share the one engine thread, so packs still serialise, and a fragment started during a drain competes with `ExportNext` in the same FIFO; the upper bound of (b)+(c) alone is the ~16% non-pack part (~45 ms per CN on q03). Packing during execution into staging leases (a, first variant) would need ~30 GB of arena per CN for q03 (15.3 GB sender-side + 14.5 GB receiver-side held 0.44-0.68 s) against 17.18 GB configured, and exhaustion is a hard failure (B6). The impact sentence "small fragments could have overlapped the lineitem scan" is wrong for the current engine (one fragment at a time, B1); only the drain itself, ~0.25-0.28 s of q03's 1.42 s span, is recoverable.
316	
317	**Proposed.** Move `export_packed` off the engine thread (needs `ParkedOutput`/`Fragment` reachable from another thread; the parked map lives on the engine thread's stack, engine.rs:262-272) and make it faster: try a larger `kPackChunkBytes` or a single `cudf::pack` for GPU-resident batches (the receiver-side copy of the same bytes is 30x faster, so the 8 MiB chunking is the suspect; inference, medium confidence). Then (b)/(c) add value. Expected gain 0.15-0.3 s per shuffle stage at 4 CNs for q03/q10/q12 (inference). Confidence high on the mechanism.
318	
319	#### B6 (confirmed). The staging arena is 87-88% full for q03 and q07 at 4 CNs, and exhaustion fails the query instead of applying backpressure
320	
321	**Measured.** cn4 q03.r1 receiver on 9102: stream 2 frames 4.8885 + 4.8423 + 4.8506 GB + 3 x 0.146 (stream 9) + 3 x 0.03 (stream 6) = 15.1 GB = 14.1 GiB of the 16 GiB arena (cn4/cluster.log `received remote batches`); Quent whole-query occupancy peak 14.95-15.10 GB of 17.18 GB per CN at +1.28 s. Frames land at +0.71..+1.01 s and are consumed at +1.30 s (dwell 0.4-0.6 s while the customer and orders x customer fragments run and the receiver waits for all four senders). q07.r1: lineitem 3 x 3.62-3.68 + orders 3 x 1.13 + customer 3 x 0.30 = ~15.2 GB per CN. q10 6.4-11.7 GiB, q12 5.4-6.0, q14 <= 3.3, q19 0.7. Lease waits are zero (cn4-transmits.txt `lease_ms` median 0, max 15 ms in q12.r1), which is consistent with a non-blocking arena, not with "no pressure". Peak lease concurrency per CN: q07.r1 63-64, q03.r1 55-56 (cn4-quent.txt per-fragment `maxconc`; session-wide max 94, WORKFLOW-PLAN fact 13) against no lease-count limit, so the arena is bounded by bytes only; per-query lease counts and GB in cn4-quent.txt are time-attributed and can bleed into the next run (tooling defect AGG-6 below), which is why per-stream bytes above come from cn4/cluster.log rather than from the lease digest.
322	
323	**Source (verified).** `src/exec/exchange_staging_arena.cpp:248` throws `exchange staging arena exhausted: requested {} bytes ... (raise SIRIUS_EXCHANGE_STAGING_BYTES)`; `nixl_transport.rs:720 rpc_request_lease(...)?` propagates the error out of the drain; `compute_node_service.rs:1302 handle_staging_lease` has no wait or retry. The arena's own destructor summary never printed because the CNs were force-exited.
324	
325	**Impact (inference, medium).** With the current FE plan the arena requirement for q03 grows as lineitem/N: ~SF1150 with `STAGING=16GiB`, or SF1000 with a 12 GiB arena, fails q03 after all the scan work is done. Broadcasting the small side (P3) would need < 1 GB of arena per CN for this family.
326	
327	**Proposed.** Short term: document `STAGING >= (N-1)/N x largest shuffled stream` in the cn-tuning guidance and fix P3. Engine: make `exchange_staging_arena::lease` block with a bounded wait on release instead of throwing, so a full arena throttles senders; or let the receiver push remote frames into pool memory on arrival (`push_packed` is already a deep copy) and release the lease immediately, keeping only the per-frame row count for `declare_input_cardinality`. Confidence high on the occupancy and the failure path.
328	
329	#### B7 (medium confidence, not adversarially verified). Per-task GPU_SCAN time rises 1.3-1.6x when four CNs scan concurrently, and at 1 CN the 4 pipeline slots bound the scan
330	
331	**Measured.** Per-task GPU_SCAN Computing (ms per ~2.2-2.3 GB task, `*-quent.json top_ops`): q03 lineitem 102 (1 CN) / 134-145 (4 CN) / 111 (standalone); q10 90 / 100-119 / 96; q12 orders 107 / 131-146 / 117; q14 151 / 240-249 / 176; q19 85 / 113-126 / 98; q07 130 / 179-186 / 142; q06 100 / 138-146. Per GB: q01 0.047 -> 0.072 s/GB, q06 0.067 -> 0.096, q13 0.322 -> 0.498. q01 additionally shows 0.5-0.87 s stalls on 10% of splits on 2-3 of the 4 CNs, varying per run, with balanced bytes per CN (agent-notes/agg-only.md section 4); the 4-CN scan fragment is 1.43x (q01) / 1.6x (q06) the ideal quarter of the 1-CN fragment, which is 26-31% of the 4-CN wall. Aggregate read rates: q01 8.2 GB/s (1 CN) vs 22.9 GB/s (4 CN); q06 20.5 vs 50.8 GB/s, so the storage has headroom over what 4 slots pull. At 1 CN all 107 (q01) / 65 (q06) scan tasks are created within 9-50 ms and the 4 slots are busy 98%+ of the fragment wall (Queued median = half the wall); the memory gate does not bind for these two.
332	
333	**Cause not identified.** The `scan_split_read` probe recorded counts only in the digest because `quent_bp.py` reads the wrong attribute keys (`bytes`/`elapsed_ns` instead of `compressed_bytes`/`output_bytes`/`materialize_ns` emitted by `src/telemetry/scan_telemetry.cpp:52-56`), and even the raw probe covers read + decode together (`materialize_ns`). Candidates: GPFS client contention on concurrent O_DIRECT streams from 16 slots, host/GPU-side effects, NUMA placement. The CN launcher cannot raise `pipeline.num_threads` because `engine_settings.rs::derive_sirius_config_yaml` emits no pipeline block (and pairs with C3: 8 slots would request 156 GB in the cold-start wave).
334	
335	**Proposed.** Split the probe into read and decode, fix the digest keys (AGG-6), then A/B `SIRIUS_CN_USE_SIRIUS_DATASOURCE=false` and buffered reads / prefetch cache with the page cache warm vs dropped; add `SIRIUS_CN_PIPELINE_THREADS` to the derived config and sweep 6 and 8 on 1 CN with Quent on.
336	
337	#### Disputed backpressure finding
338	
339	**BJ-6: "memory backpressure is absent for q03/q10/q12/q14/q19 at both 1 and 4 CN; the 6-15x over-reservation is harmless because concurrent reservations are far below the pool": refuted on the 1-CN half and on the mechanism; the conclusion (memory pressure is not this family's loss) stands.** Objection (data skeptic, agent-notes/refute-bj6): 4 concurrent tasks hold 58-80% of the 107.37 GB limit, not "far below"; the reservation gate blocked 47-178 ms per run in q10/q12/q14 at 1 CN in all three runs (see C3), 0 at 4 CNs and standalone; the engine pool's running peak reached 92-99% of the limit inside q03.r0 and q04.r0. "No arena exhaustion" is vacuous evidence because exhaustion is a hard failure, never backpressure (B6). The proposed regression guard is inverted: a tighter estimate reduces gating; guard instead that `num_threads x per-task cold-start request` stays well under the limit. Cost today is <= 0.18 s per query, so the impact ranking (planning, CN serialisation, scan contention dominate) survives.
340	
341	#### Tooling defects found on the way (AGG-6, high confidence)
342	
343	`scratchpad/perf/sf1000/quent_bp.py:98-104` attributes staging leases by a +-0.5 s time window, so the last run of each query inherits the next cold run's first leases (cn4 q06.r2 shows 55 leases / 25.6 GB although q06 moves 64 bytes per stream; cn4-quent.txt per-fragment lease counts are likewise attributed by time, e.g. q07.r1's 1-task nation fragment shows 184 leases). Use cn4-cnlog.json per-stream transmit bytes for volume. `quent_bp.py:60-70 scan_reads` uses the wrong keys (see B7). Fix both before the next capture.
344	
345	---
346	
347	## 4. What to do first
348	
349	Ordered by value per unit of work, with the expected effect and the risk. "Measured" effects are computed from this campaign's numbers; everything else is inference.
350	
351	| # | change | where | expected effect | risk / caveat | confidence |
352	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
353	| 1 | Fail fast in the OOM reschedule loop when the downgrade freed 0 bytes, usage == limit and the retry floor exceeds the grantable reservation (B3) | `src/pipeline/gpu_pipeline_executor.cpp:263` (reservation gate) or `:330-420` (reschedule path) | the six failures die in ~3 s instead of 54-232 s (measured: 775 s of the 910 s sweep); the error names the real cause | keep the 100-retry budget for the cross-GPU contention case (arrives via `rmm::out_of_memory`, not the gate); needs `freed`/`global_usage` plumbed into the reschedule path if implemented there | high |
354	| 2 | Per-query parked-output bookkeeping: drop only the failed query's slots, skip its pending `Run`s, drop slots on cancel and on pre-run translation failure (B4) | `experimental/starrocks/src/engine.rs:291-316, ~626-643`; `compute_node_service.rs:449-476, 864-905, 1325-1400`; `local_exchange.rs` | removes the 0-38 GB leaks (measured) and 0.4-6.4 s of stolen engine time per failure; restores order-independence of results | Err-time bookkeeping is required (cancel arrives after the next sender started) | high |
355	| 3 | Real FILES() cardinalities in the FE: (a) bytes / row width from `TableFunctionTable.fileStatuses`, FE-only; (b) exact `num_rows` via a new field in `PGetFileSchemaResult` filled from `file_schema.rs` (C1) | `StatisticsCalculator.java:664-676`; `TableFunctionTable.java:300, 611, 688-712`; `internal_service.proto:647-650`; `file_schema.rs:19-27` | correct build sides, broadcast of the small dimensions (nation/region/supplier), q12/q19 broadcast at 4 CNs, re-armed `broadcast_row_limit`; prerequisite for every other plan-shape fix | alone it does not undo the six 1-CN failures (broadcast memory penalty and 0 single-node shuffle cost, P1) nor flip q03/q10 (guard, P3); needs `EXPLAIN COSTS` verification, and likely a GPU-sized `broadcast_row_limit` / `exec_mem_limit` | medium-high on the change, medium on outcomes |
356	| 4 | Make the six queries runnable on 1 CN: either (a) same-node fragment fusion before translation, or (b) parked repositories visible to the downgrade sweep + HOST-tier `output_row_count`/`export_packed` (P1, B1, B2) | (a) `compute_node_service.rs process_fragment` / `local_exchange.rs register_receiver` at the `TPlan` level; (b) `src/exec/streaming_fragment.cpp:103-112`, `src/downgrade/downgrade_executor.cpp:223-232`, `src/sirius_ffi.cpp:822-825, 1062-1066` | (a) reproduces the standalone plan that passes all six at 2.7-6.4 s; (b) five of six would plausibly pass slowly (q09 marginal at ~253 GB vs 279 GB GPU+HOST) | (a) substantial; 1-CN only; q21 also needs #5; (b) medium effort; spill throughput unknown | medium |

368	---
369	
370	## 5. Open questions and what was not measured
371	
372	1. **4-CN behaviour of q05 q08 q09 q17 q18 q21.** Never run (cn4/runs/runs.csv). The per-CN parked lineitem share would be ~31-61 GB, so passing is expected, but q09's per-CN share (61 GB) plus its other shuffled streams is untested, and the 4-CN plans differ in shape (q21).

---- apply script
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Re-applies Sirius-only patches onto the vendored StarRocks checkout.
# Safe to re-run: skips a patch that already applies (or is already present).
set -euo pipefail

root="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
submodule="$root/starrocks"
patch_dir="$root/patches"

if [[ ! -f "$submodule/gensrc/proto/internal_service.proto" ]]; then
  echo "StarRocks submodule is not checked out at $submodule" >&2
  echo "Run: git submodule update --init --recursive experimental/starrocks/starrocks" >&2
  exit 1
fi

shopt -s nullglob
patches=("$patch_dir"/*.patch)
if ((${#patches[@]} == 0)); then
  echo "No patches under $patch_dir" >&2
  exit 1
fi

cd "$submodule"
for patch in "${patches[@]}"; do
  if git apply --check "$patch" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    git apply "$patch"
    echo "applied $(basename "$patch")"
  elif git apply --reverse --check "$patch" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "already applied $(basename "$patch")"
  else
    echo "failed to apply $(basename "$patch")" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
done

      - uses: prefix-dev/setup-pixi@f00437f565399d418b0acc85936d12c1fb668347 # v0.10.1
        with:
          cache: false
          pixi-version: v0.71.1
          manifest-path: experimental/starrocks/pixi.toml
          environments: cn

      # Scope by package: `--all` would also reach the sibling rust/ workspace via the
      # `sirius` path dep. Mirrors check.yml's scoped rust/ fmt check.
      - name: fmt
        run: pixi run -e cn cargo fmt --package sirius-starrocks-cn --package starrocks-plan-translator --package starrocks-thrift -- --check

      # The CN's `sirius-engine` feature is on by default but links a Sirius build
      # tree (C++ toolchain + RAPIDS/CUDA) that this CI env does not have, so build
      # the pure-Rust path here. The engine path is exercised on a GPU box via
      # `pixi run cn-build` / `cn-test`.
      - name: clippy
        run: pixi run -e cn cargo clippy --all-targets --no-default-features -- -D warnings

      - name: test
        run: pixi run -e cn cargo test --workspace --no-default-features

    steps:

# Cluster: 100GiB GPU pool, 16GiB staging, 160GiB host per CN (the perf plan's retime configuration), watchdog 300 s,
# Quent on with per-fragment labels, async sender dispatch on. Telemetry dirs are wiped before launch so the newest
# session per CN is this arm's; after a clean SIGTERM the sessions are copied to <out>/quent/cn<i>/.
SP=/tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad
WT=/home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius-stacks-wt/perf; SR=$WT/experimental/starrocks; DATA=/scratch/sirius/datasets/tpch_sf1000
N=$1; TAG=$2; TO=$3; RUNS=$4; shift 4
OUT=$SP/perf/sf1000/$TAG; mkdir -p $OUT/quent
source $SP/cluster-env.sh $WT
export NUM_CNS=$N GPU_MEM=100GiB HOST_MEM=160GiB STAGING=16GiB SIRIUS_EXCHANGE_STAGING_BYTES=16GiB SIRIUS_QUERY_WATCHDOG_SECS=300
export SIRIUS_CN_ENABLE_QUENT=1 SIRIUS_CN_ASYNC_SENDER_DISPATCH=1
[ "$N" = 1 ] && { export SIRIUS_CN_DUMP_FRAGMENTS=$OUT/dump; mkdir -p $OUT/dump; rm -f $OUT/dump/*; }
M="mysql --host 127.0.0.1 --port 9030 --user root --batch --connect-timeout=5"
echo "##### CAPTURE $TAG NUM_CNS=$N queries: $* $(date -u +%T)"
pgrep -f "$SR/target/release/sirius-starrocks-cn" >/dev/null && { echo "REFUSING: CNs from this worktree still running"; exit 2; }
rm -rf $SR/.cn*/telemetry/*
bash $SP/start-cluster.sh $WT $OUT/cluster.log
for i in $(seq 1 60); do n=$($M -e "SHOW COMPUTE NODES;" 2>/dev/null | awk -F'\t' 'NR==1{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++) if($i=="Alive") c=i; next} $c=="true"{n++} END{print n+0}'); [ "$n" = "$N" ] && break; sleep 3; done
echo "alive=$n after $((i*3))s"; nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,memory.used --format=csv,noheader | tr '\n' ' '; echo
bash $SP/perf/sf1000/run-queries.sh $TAG $DATA $OUT/runs $TO $RUNS "$@"
echo "== stopping (SIGTERM, wait) $(date -u +%T)"; bash $SP/stop-cluster.sh $WT
for d in $SR/.cn*; do cn=$(basename $d); [ -d $d/telemetry ] || continue; for s in $d/telemetry/*/; do mkdir -p $OUT/quent/$cn; cp -r $s $OUT/quent/$cn/; done; done
grep -a "/\* $TAG " $SR/starrocks/output/fe/log/fe.audit.log 2>/dev/null | sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' > $OUT/fe.audit.$TAG.log
echo "audit lines with marker: $(wc -l < $OUT/fe.audit.$TAG.log); quent sessions: $(ls -d $OUT/quent/*/*/ 2>/dev/null | wc -l)"
echo "##### CAPTURE $TAG DONE $(date -u +%T)"

# OOM-5 refutation check (post-failure parked-output leak)

Files produced here: cn-events.txt (ANSI-stripped CN events from cn1/cluster.log with line numbers),
pool-trace.txt (engine-cn0.log [gpu_pool] QueryBegin/End 13:02-13:19:30, GB), headroom.txt (per run: baseline at
start, max allocated at any fragment boundary, own peak, headroom to the 107.37 GB cap).

## Mechanism: CONFIRMED (code + logs)
- compute_node_service.rs:449-478 cancel_plan_fragment only calls results.cancel(); comment says real teardown is a
  separate work item. run_ready_fragment (:862-905) on receiver failure calls results.fail_query() only; no parked drop,
  no per-query skip. engine.rs:278-300: engine thread serves Run requests one at a time; parked/parked_slots are cleared
  only when run_fragment returns Err (process-wide wipe).
- cluster.log: after every `fragment run failed` the not-yet-run senders of the same query still start and finish:
  q05 (13:05:24.632-25.355: ..5773, ..5777, ..5776, ..5775 [inputs=2, drains streams 1 and 4]), q08 (13:08:29.792-30.836),
  q09 (13:12:22.333-22.721: ..947 ..946 ..945 ..944), q17 (13:14:56.819-13:15:03.233: two senders, one 6343 ms),
  q21 (13:18:07.604-10.954: two fragments, one inputs=1 draining stream 6 = 730,806,711 rows, 3153 ms), q18: none left.
- q16 (translator error at 13:13:12.910) ran two senders BEFORE the failure (ff87 partsupp 6.6 GB, ff86 supplier); the
  failure never went through run_fragment Err so they were not wiped (dump fragment-0421/-0422 identify the tables).

## Numbers: reproduce (pool-trace.txt)

End q=335 104.24 @13:08:29.784 -> 0.00 -> 0.08 -> 7.54 -> 8.78 -> 8.83 (q09 lineitem sender q=351 begins at 8.83, not 8.78).

q16: 31.56 -> 38.16 (q=649, 108 ms). q17 lineitem sender q=653 Begin 38.16 @13:13:13.067, End 104.42 @13:14:56.804.
End q=653 104.42 -> 0.00 -> 0.00 -> 4.00 (q17 leftover aca1, 6343 ms) -> q18 own 7.94 / 31.94 / 68.69 -> End 104.56.
End q=665 104.56 @13:15:51.013 -> 0.00, nothing leaked into q19/q20.
End q=764 103.14 @13:18:07.590 -> 0.00 -> 5.94 -> 36.64 (q21 leftovers) : q22 baseline 36.64 (not cited by analyst).

## Causal claim "directly caused q17 to die with only 66 GB parked": REFUTED
- q17 lineitem sender aca3 = dump fragment-0427 (FILE_SCAN lineitem, 32 scan ranges, no filter); CN parked 25 batches =
  66.26 GB (cn1-quent.txt q17.r0 STREAMING_SINK in=66.26GB) => 2.65 GB/batch; analyst counts 25 done + 21 stuck = 46 tasks.
- Standalone same projection: GPU_SCAN(3) n=46 in=122.25 GB (agent-notes/standalone-failed-quent.txt q17.r0/r1).
- 46 x 2.65 = 122 GB > 107.37 GB pool cap: the sender cannot be parked in a clean pool either. The leak changed when q17
  died (after 25 batches instead of ~40), not whether.
- Same for the other five: q05 171.0, q08 195.75, q09 244.5, q18 97.5 (+64.7 GB own other senders), q21 123.0 (+77.76 own)
  GB (analyst's own table, section 2 of oom-failures.md). No failure in this campaign is attributable to the leak.
- No pass/fail flip either: all 15 passing queries passed while carrying 4.69 (q06,q07), 31.56 (q10-q15), 36.64 (q22) GB.

## Corrections
- "leaks 5-38 GB": measured range is 0-36.64 GB (q18 -> 0; q17 -> 4.00; q05 -> 4.69; q08 -> 8.83; q09 -> 31.56; q21 -> 36.64).
- "partsupp scan parked 415.757 s": 415.757 s is dwell_sum over 4 batches (3 partsupp + 1 supplier); dwell_max = 103.95 s

- 8.78 -> the baseline when q09's lineitem sender started was 8.83 GB (105.24 - 8.83 = 96.41 GB parked by it).

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Map CN cluster.log events to (query, run) using runs.csv start times, then summarize per run:
fragments (role, inputs/outputs, elapsed), declared input stream cardinalities, relayed batches, nixl transmits
(bytes, elapsed/lease/write ms, gbps), failures/cancels. usage: cnlog_extract.py <cluster.log> <runs.csv> [--json out]"""
import re, sys, csv, json, collections, datetime
log, runs = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
jout = sys.argv[sys.argv.index('--json') + 1] if '--json' in sys.argv else None
import glob as _glob
engine_logs = _glob.glob(sys.argv[sys.argv.index('--engine') + 1]) if '--engine' in sys.argv else []
ANSI = re.compile(r'\x1b\[[0-9;]*m')
def ts(s):
    return datetime.datetime.strptime(s[:23], '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%f').replace(tzinfo=datetime.timezone.utc).timestamp()
R = list(csv.DictReader(open(runs)))
windows = []
for i, r in enumerate(R):
    t0 = ts(r['start_utc']); t1 = ts(R[i + 1]['start_utc']) if i + 1 < len(R) else t0 + float(r['ms']) / 1000 + 5
    windows.append((t0, t1, f"{r['query']}.r{r['run']}", r))
def which(t):
    for t0, t1, name, r in windows:
        if t0 - 0.5 <= t < t1: return name
    return None
qid_run = {}; per = collections.defaultdict(lambda: {"fragments": [], "cardinalities": [], "relayed": [], "transmits": [], "failures": [], "cancels": 0, "other_warn": collections.Counter()})
lines = [ANSI.sub('', l) for l in open(log, errors='replace')]
TS = re.compile(r'^(\d{4}-\d\d-\d\dT\d\d:\d\d:\d\d\.\d+)Z')
for l in lines:
    m = TS.match(l)
    if not m: continue
    t = ts(m.group(1)); q = re.search(r'query_id=(?:Some\(FragmentInstanceId\()?([0-9a-f-]{36})', l)
    if not q: continue
    qid = q.group(1)
    if 'fragment run started' in l:
        run = which(t); qid_run.setdefault(qid, run)
    run = qid_run.get(qid) or which(t)
    if run is None: continue
    p = per[run]
    if 'fragment run started' in l:
        p["fragments"].append({"qid": qid[-12:], "fid": re.search(r'fragment_instance_id=([0-9a-f-]{36})', l).group(1)[-12:], "role": re.search(r'role="(\w+)"', l).group(1),
                               "cn": re.search(r'cn=(\S+)', l).group(1), "inputs": int(re.search(r'inputs=(\d+)', l).group(1)), "outputs": int(re.search(r'outputs=(\d+)', l).group(1)), "t_start": t})
    elif 'fragment run finished' in l or 'fragment run failed' in l:
        fid = re.search(r'fragment_instance_id=([0-9a-f-]{36})', l).group(1)[-12:]
        for f in p["fragments"]:
            if f["fid"] == fid and "elapsed_ms" not in f:
                f["elapsed_ms"] = int(re.search(r'elapsed_ms=(\d+)', l).group(1)); f["status"] = "failed" if 'failed' in l else "ok"
                if 'failed' in l: p["failures"].append(re.search(r'error=(.*)', l).group(1)[:300])
    elif 'declared input stream cardinality' in l:
        p["cardinalities"].append({"fid": re.search(r'fragment_instance_id=([0-9a-f-]{36})', l).group(1)[-12:], "stream": int(re.search(r'stream_id=(\d+)', l).group(1)), "rows": int(re.search(r'rows=(\d+)', l).group(1))})
    elif 'relayed native batches' in l:
        p["relayed"].append({"stream": int(re.search(r'stream_id=(\d+)', l).group(1)), "sender": int(re.search(r'sender_id=(\d+)', l).group(1)), "batches": int(re.search(r'batches=(\d+)', l).group(1))})
    elif 'transmitted batches via nixl' in l:
        g = lambda k: (lambda m: m.group(1) if m else None)(re.search(k + r'="?([0-9.]+)"?', l))
        p["transmits"].append({"stream": g('stream_id'), "sender": g('sender_id'), "dest": (re.search(r'dest=(\S+)', l) or [None, None])[1], "batches": g('batches'), "bytes": g('bytes'), "elapsed_ms": g('elapsed_ms'), "lease_ms": g('lease_ms'), "write_ms": g('write_ms'), "write_gbps": g('write_gbps')})
    elif 'cancel_plan_fragment' in l: p["cancels"] += 1
    elif 'WARN' in l or 'ERROR' in l: p["other_warn"][re.sub(r'[0-9a-f-]{36}|\d+', 'N', l.split(': ', 2)[-1])[:120]] += 1
# engine (C++) logs: "[2026-09-03 13:03:44.795] [warning] [gpu_pipeline_executor.cpp:366] ... reschedule (retry 1/100) ... OOM at operator X"
eng = collections.defaultdict(lambda: {"oom_reschedules": 0, "oom_ops": collections.Counter(), "retry_exhausted": 0, "reservation_failed": 0, "reservation_clamped": 0, "downgrade": 0})
ETS = re.compile(r'^\[(\d{4}-\d\d-\d\d) (\d\d:\d\d:\d\d\.\d+)\]')
for el in engine_logs:
    for l in open(el, errors='replace'):
        m = ETS.match(l)
        if not m: continue
        t = ts(m.group(1) + 'T' + m.group(2)); run = which(t)
        if run is None: continue
        e = eng[run]
        if 'reschedule (retry' in l:
            e["oom_reschedules"] += 1; mo = re.search(r'OOM at operator (\S+)', l); e["oom_ops"][mo.group(1) if mo else '?'] += 1
        elif 'exceeded' in l and 'retries' in l: e["retry_exhausted"] += 1
        elif 'Failed to acquire memory reservation' in l: e["reservation_failed"] += 1
        elif 'clamping reservation request' in l: e["reservation_clamped"] += 1
        elif 'downgrade' in l.lower(): e["downgrade"] += 1
out = {}
for t0, t1, name, r in windows:
    p = per.get(name); 
    if not p: out[name] = {"status": r['status'], "ms": int(r['ms']), "note": "no CN events mapped"}; continue

45dab3be45f3b26992aedf8facb062937aa56d83
feat(telemetry): Quent events for scan reads, stream hops, staging leases and CN fragment labels
A fragment data-flow model needs, with timestamps and bytes, the query a fragment
belongs to, each scan split's read, every hop between fragments and the staging
arena's leases. Quent had the plan, tasks and data batches but none of those.
Scan splits now emit an Operator `statistics` event `scan_split_read` (sources,
compressed and output bytes, rows, materialize time) on the scan pipeline.
Fragment::relay_from and push_packed register BatchPlacements with origin
`stream_relayed` / `stream_pushed`, and the wire batch built by push_packed gets a
real DataBatch. The exchange staging arena is a Quent Memory with Channels to and
from every memory space; each lease is a DataBatch `staging_lease` that goes
InTransit on export_packed (GPU to arena) and push_packed (arena to GPU). All
probes are no-ops without a telemetry context.

The compute node writes `enable_quent` explicitly (off unless --enable-quent or
SIRIUS_CN_ENABLE_QUENT=1), names its engine by its exchange identity, and labels
every fragment `<query id>:<fragment instance id>` through the new
Fragment::set_query_label; nixl sends and receives and fragment start/end are
logged with those ids as the documented stitch until they can be Quent events.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

9a5a4da6c8bed942db3a1df8f64d404226c6f414
perf(cn): opt-in async dispatch of sender-only fragments
exec_plan_fragment ran a sender fragment inside the RPC and replied only after
the scan and its remote drains finished. The FE deploys the first fragment
instance of every node in one wave and waits for those replies, so on a gather
plan the node that also hosts the merge fragment received its own scan one full
scan later: on 4 CNs at SF1000 three q06 scans started together and the fourth
726 ms after them. With SIRIUS_CN_ASYNC_SENDER_DISPATCH=1 a fragment with no
exchange input and no RESULT_SINK is queued on the dispatch worker and the RPC
returns at once. Off by default: a queued sender's failure only reaches result
instances reserved on its own node, and the inline contract stays the tested
default until a sender failure is forwarded to the receiver's node.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run bench-kit TPC-H queries against the FE on 9030 with a /* marker */ so the FE audit log ties QueryId to (query, run).
# usage: run-queries.sh <tag> <tpch_data> <out_dir> <timeout_s> <runs_after_warmup> q01 q02 ...
# writes <out_dir>/runs.csv (query,run,phase,status,ms,rows,start_utc) and <out_dir>/<q>.r<i>.out (mysql --batch)
TAG=$1; DATA=$2; OUT=$3; TO=$4; RUNS=$5; shift 5
QD=/home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius-stacks-wt/perf/experimental/starrocks/benchmarks/tpch/queries
mkdir -p $OUT; echo "query,run,phase,status,ms,rows,start_utc" > $OUT/runs.csv
M="mysql --host 127.0.0.1 --port 9030 --user root --batch --connect-timeout=5"
for q in "$@"; do
  sql=$(sed "s#__TPCH_DATA__#$DATA#g" $QD/$q.sql)
  for i in $(seq 0 $RUNS); do
    phase=warm; [ $i = 0 ] && phase=cold
    start=$(date -u +%FT%T.%3N); t0=$(date +%s%N)
    if timeout $TO $M -e "/* $TAG $q r$i */ $sql" > $OUT/$q.r$i.out 2> $OUT/$q.r$i.err; then st=pass; else st=fail; rc=$?; fi
    ms=$(( ($(date +%s%N) - t0) / 1000000 )); rows=$(( $(wc -l < $OUT/$q.r$i.out) - 1 )); [ $rows -lt 0 ] && rows=0
    [ $st = fail ] && [ $ms -ge $((TO*1000 - 500)) ] && st=timeout
    echo "$q,$i,$phase,$st,$ms,$rows,$start" >> $OUT/runs.csv
    echo "$q r$i $phase $st ${ms}ms rows=$rows $( [ $st != pass ] && head -c 160 $OUT/$q.r$i.err | tr '\n' ' ')"
    [ $st != pass ] && break   # a failing run skips the rest of that query (bench.sh semantics)
  done
done

input.title: fix(cn): retire a failed query's parked output instead of wiping every query's
input.summary: Base is the upstream design (judge 1's winner; judge 2's "surgical plus two mandatory upstream merges" converges on the same core). Parked sender output on the CN becomes query-scoped: a new CI-compiled `parked_registry.rs` (`ParkedRegistry<F>` + bounded `RetiredQueries`) replaces the three loose maps in engine.rs, the process-wide wipe at engine.rs:291-316 becomes a per-query `retire`, and a shared `Arc<Mutex<RetiredQueries>>` marked on the engine thread (or by `SiriusEngine::retire_query` before a fire-and-forget `RetireQuery` request) refuses already-queued runs in both dispatch modes. Four gates: refusal as the first statement inside `run_fragment_inner` so the remote-input lease sweep at engine.rs:462-478 still runs; a park-time refusal for output finished after its query was retired; a dispatch-worker gate at the top of `run_ready_fragment` that releases staged batches and emits no `fragment run started`; an arrival gate in `process_fragment` that keeps the result-fragment reserve-then-fail contract. `fail_fragment` (fail_query + retire_query) covers the q16 translation case, and a `StagedLeases` drop guard releases arena leases on every pre-run error path. Commit 2 makes `cancel_plan_fragment` a real teardown (every reason retires parked + rendezvous state via `LocalExchange::retire_receiver`/`is_retired` with a HashSet twin; only failure reasons record `cancel_query`), refuses late remote frames, and records inline-path failures at query level. Merged from robust: `AlreadyTornDown` idempotent release, structured retire log fields, the `skipping fragment of a retired query` grep target. Merged from surgical: RetiredQueries capacity 1024, the unlabelled-failure GPU test, the cancel-reason matrix test, the acceptance arithmetic. Not merged: TTL sweep, knobs, Inventory, fail_query_all, three-PR split. One correction to upstream's split: the RetireQuery request belongs in commit 1 because fail_fragment needs it. No engine C++, FE, proto or knob changes; two commits, ~550 non-test + ~800 test lines, ~2 engineer-days + one GPU session.
